Netanyahu Considering Crypto Plan to Dodge Banking Sanctions on Israel - Decrypt
text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he has asked for a plan to use cryptocurrency and blockchain networks to help Israel get around possible banking sanctions. He made the comments in an interview on Israel’s Channel 10, four days before the country votes in a national election.
Apparently, Netanyahu is somewhat confident that the United States will stop providing Israel with military funding. “It is only a question of time.” he said, telling Israelis to get used to the idea of not continuing to “receive tens of billions of dollars in American assistance” for the country’s defense budget.
“There could be sanctions, including banking sanctions,” he continued. “You have to prepare an alternative economy and think about currencies that can get around those restrictions. I am working on that as well.”
One of the alternatives is using crypto and decentralized technologies.
“Blockchain is one of the alternatives, certainly,” Netanyahu said when asked if it could be a way around sanctions. “I have already asked for a plan to be prepared for that.”
Netanyahu did not elaborate on who is drafting the plan, what currency or network it would use, or when it would be ready. If approved, Israel would be joining a small list of countries that have already tried a similar approach, including Venezuela, Iran, Russia, North Korea, all of which have used crypto to move funds outside of America’s intervention.
Netanyahu’s approach of a blockchain plan resembles Venezuela’s president Nicolas Maduro’s, who not only drew a plan but also designed a whole legal system around that idea.
Venezuela has used Tether and Bitcoin to sustain its oil industry, and created the Petro in an effort to push its whole economy outside of the SWIFT.
Russia tried a similar route with A7A5, a ruble-pegged token from a payments firm co-owned by a sanctioned state bank. It moved about $102 billion in its first year, per Elliptic, before sanctions and a hack of its main exchange cut its daily volume by 96% from its peak. Israel’s largest bank, Bank Leumi, plans to offer Bitcoin trading in early 2027 through Galaxy Digital, pending Bank of Israel approval.
Banking sanctions mean foreign banks refuse to process payments for a country’s banks, which makes it harder for importers to pay suppliers and eventually pushes up prices at the supermarket.
More than 60 Israeli economists and former officials warned this week that measures now aimed at West Bank settlements could spread to the wider economy and raise the cost of living, per Ynet.
The U.K. banned imports from Israeli settlements in early September and announced sanctions on people and companies involved in building them. Eleven other countries, including France and Canada, said they intend to restrict trade in settlement goods.
The pressure follows the war in Gaza. A UN commission of inquiry—an independent panel that does not speak for the UN itself—concluded in September 2025 that Israel was committing genocide there. The International Criminal Court separately issued arrest warrants in November 2024 for Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, which Netanyahu has said Israel will not recognize.
Roy Katz, the Channel 10 broadcaster, also asked whether Netanyahu worries about what happens after Donald Trump leaves office, even if Vice President J.D. Vance succeeds him. Netanyahu did not mention Trump losing power, but his answer was about a world without him.
“I can say with certainty that there has never been a president as friendly to Israel as Trump, and there may never be another like him,” Netanyahu said. “We must prepare for a rainy day. I want independence in weapons production, just as I wanted energy independence.”
Earlier in the same interview, Netanyahu had tied Israel’s markets to Trump. “The markets know that if I win, we will proceed together with President Trump,” he said. “He said he would work only with me.”
If Trump loses, Natanyahu named India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi as one partner already discussing cooperation.
“India, a country led by my friend Narendra Modi, is also discussing cooperation with us in production,” Netanyahu said “I won’t give details; I’d rather implement things first and take credit afterward.”
Crypto is not an easy escape from sanctions, because blockchains are public and traceable. On July 1, Defense Minister Israel Katz signed sanctions orders on 37 crypto wallets holding more than 24 million shekels that Israel says belong to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and were meant to fund Hezbollah, and the head of the ministry’s counter-terror financing bureau said there is “no immunity for terror financiers even in the crypto sphere.”
Tether, the company behind the dollar-pegged USDT stablecoin, can freeze any wallet holding its token. It froze $344 million in April working with U.S. authorities, and in July it froze $131 million in wallets tied to Iran’s central bank and armed forces after U.S. sanctions.
Israelis vote on October 27, and the current U.S. military aid agreement expires in September 2028, just before the next presidential election in the United States.

title: Phantom rolls out Kalshi prediction markets to US users, says it's 'confident and comfortable' amid state lawsuits
text: Crypto wallet provider Phantom is rolling out Kalshi prediction markets to U.S. users, letting them trade event contracts directly on its app. The rollout begins Friday, Oct. 23, with access expanding over the coming weeks. Phantom users will need to complete KYC on Kalshi. The launch comes as states challenge Kalshi's claim that federal oversight protects its event contract offerings from state gambling laws. Asked whether those disputes raised concerns for Phantom, General Counsel Kevin Jacobs said the company was comfortable moving forward. "Our perspective is that the CFTC’s jurisdiction here is clear," Jacobs told The Block. "So long as our interaction with these products is consistent with our no-action position, we are confident and comfortable engaging in this activity," he said. In March, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued Phantom a conditional " no action " letter, relieving it from registering as a broker. Then, last month, the CFTC extended that relief to other software providers. Jacobs said Phantom would comply with state restrictions while the disputes play out, adding that he expects the Supreme Court will eventually have the final say. Market access and fees Phantom said it will initially be blocking sports markets in Michigan; sports, elections, politics and entertainment in Nevada; and those plus culture, science and tech, mentions and geopolitics in Washington. Those restrictions could change as their respective cases play out in court. Kalshi is making its full catalog available to Phantom, with Phantom deciding which markets to display, Max Crowley, Kalshi's vice president of business development, told The Block. Crowley declined to comment on the active state cases. Users will be able to fund trades with CASH, Phantom's dollar-pegged stablecoin, through their Phantom Cash accounts. Jacobs added that "more ways to pay are coming soon." Funds move to Kalshi and are converted into fiat for settlement, while cash outs and winnings return to users' Cash accounts. Phantom quoted a prediction feed of $0.02 per contract, plus a small network fee for moving funds to Kalshi. Users will see a breakdown before confirming a trade or cash-out. Crowley said he expects the partnership will bring more users to Kalshi, increase liquidity and improve its market data. Kalshi has recorded more than $291 billion in trading volume this year, according to The Block data. October volume has reached $55.33 billion with nine days left in the month, putting it on pace to surpass September's monthly record of $59.32 billion. Kalshi monthly volume year to date. Netanyahu Says Blockchain Could Help Israel Evade to Sanctions
text:
Ahead of elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel could turn to blockchain and crypto to skirt potential international sanctions, to the dismay of opponents and the country’s central banker.
Blockchain has become an issue in this week’s Israeli elections after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that the country could turn to cryptocurrency to avoid strains on the economy from any potential international financial sanctions.
He told a local television interviewer that Israel is exploring the use of blockchain technology and cryptocurrencies as a means of circumventing potential banking sanctions.
“Blockchain is an alternative to sanctions,” the prime minister said in an interview with Israel’s Channel 10 economic network on Friday.
His calling blockchain a “national strategic tool” signals a pivot in the government’s stance on the digital currency industry, from an investment event into part of the country’s economic defense strategy, reported CryptoJungle, Israel’s largest crypto media platform.
A dozen Western countries have announced sanctions targeting goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank in response to Jewish settler attacks on Palestinians and an increase in settlement construction approved by Netanyahu’s right-wing government. Those sanctions could extend into Israel proper, economists and industry figures told The Times of Israel last month.
Several of the candidates seeking to replace Netanyahu in the Oct. 27 elections, as well as the head of the Bank of Israel, were quick to challenge the prime minister’s statement.
“The BibiCoin vision is a threat to national security,” wrote Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot in a Saturday morning X post, using a play on Netanyahu’s nickname. The Bank of Israel in a statement rejected Netanyahu’s proposition, saying that cryptocurrencies “cannot be used as a route for bypassing sanctions.”

At Saturday evening’s anti-government rally in Tel Aviv, several onlookers weighed in on Netanyahu’s blockchain statement.
“An economy that runs on the dark web makes us no better than our enemies,” said Aryeh Cohen, holding a sign that said in English “enough Bibi’s B.S.” Another rally attendee who gave only her first name, Pnina, told Cointelegraph “what’s next, the Bank of Israel living ‘neath the law.”
Media critics also lambasted the idea of use of crypto to skirt sanctions.
“The crypto element deserves particular scrutiny. Digital currencies can indeed move value outside some traditional banking channels,” wrote Yediot Ahronot columnist Nadav Eyal in an X post. “But they are not a substitute for a national financial system. They don’t provide credit lines to banks, they don’t replace international capital markets, and they don’t persuade foreign companies to violate sanctions that bar them from doing business with Israel.”
“Crypto & blockchain-based solutions are not the tool for bypassing sanctions,” Ben Samocha, founder of CryptoJungle, told Cointelegraph on Sunday. “As demonstrated by the US Treasury against Iran, blockchain investigation allows tracking illicit funds, blocking their fiat gateway, and even freezing them.” He said that the Israeli economy is not fit to bypass sanctions using crypto.

title: Senate Democrat Probes Tether Payments to Ex-White House Crypto Adviser’s Firm - Decrypt
text:
Tether is facing fresh scrutiny in the Senate over millions of dollars that reportedly flowed to a firm co-owned by Bo Hines while he helped shape U.S. stablecoin law at the White House.
Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., the top Democrat on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, sent Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino a letter Thursday demanding records of the company’s dealings with Hines and Nxum, the consulting firm he co-founded. Blumenthal gave Tether until Nov. 3 to respond.
Hines was executive director of President Donald Trump’s Presidential Council of Advisers for Digital Assets and a key architect of the GENIUS Act, signed in July 2025. He left the White House on Aug. 9, 2025, and Tether named him CEO of its new U.S. division the following month.
Blumenthal’s letter builds on an Oct. 14 Wall Street Journal investigation. The Journal reported that Nxum has earned $6.3 million from a deal Tether struck in May 2025. Tether agreed to pay a marketing firm, Notorious, $415,000 a month, and the firm passed most of the first payment to a wallet used by Nxum, where it was split three ways. Later payments went directly to Nxum after Hines left government. Hines kept his one-third stake in Nxum while serving in the White House, the Journal reported.
The Journal also reported that Hines urged lawmakers to double the law’s compliance window from 18 to 36 months, a change that chiefly benefited Tether. Messages it reviewed showed Hines sharing talking points about Republican holdouts with his Nxum partners. After a call from Ardoino, Hines’ father and Nxum co-owner, Todd Hines, wrote: “They want us to obliterate these members that are fighting crypto.”
A Nxum representative told the Journal that Hines wasn’t involved in the Tether deal while in government and “did not receive any Tether-derived funds during that period.”
“Tether is aware of the allegations reported in The Wall Street Journal that form the basis of Senator Blumenthal’s letter,” Tether today said in a statement. “External counsel previously conducted an in-depth internal investigation into the matter, which found no evidence of wrongdoing.”
Blumenthal wrote that the payment structure suggests Tether “was likely well aware of the illegality and impropriety” of paying a sitting official, and that the arrangement “implicates federal ethics, anticorruption, and lobbying laws.” He also asked about a Nxum pitch deck, reported by the Journal, saying Tether would buy a 25% stake in the firm for $56 million.
It’s Blumenthal’s second Tether-linked letter this month. On Oct. 8, he asked Cantor Fitzgerald, Tether’s reserve custodian and a 5% shareholder chaired by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s son, for records on that relationship.
That letter followed a report from his staff finding that most Iran-linked wallets used USDT. Tether responded by citing about $550 million in Iran-linked freezes, including $344 million in April.
Lutnick defended Tether at his confirmation hearing last year, and Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Ron Wyden pressed him in April over a reported Tether loan to a trust for his children.

title: Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand central banks expand cross-border stablecoin initiative involving Ripple, Visa and Mastercard
text: The central banks of Malaysia and Thailand are joining Singapore's BLOOM (Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online, Multi-currency) initiative to work on cross-border payments involving stablecoins and tokenized deposits. Singapore's Monetary Authority (MAS) confirmed Friday that Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank of Thailand had joined as policymaker members. Ripple, Visa, Mastercard, and the World Bank Group are also among the initiative's participants, alongside Circle, Coinbase, JPMorgan, Standard Chartered, and Stripe. BLOOM began in October last year, with MAS bringing together banks and technology firms to test payments using tokenized bank money and regulated stablecoins. Singapore has separately tested a wholesale central bank digital currency. Cross-border payments and settlement Ripple first announced its participation in BLOOM in March, when it said it would test trade payments using RLUSD on the XRP Ledger. The trial with supply chain fintech firm Unloq uses its SC+ platform to automate payment releases when predefined conditions are met. MAS said the work will focus on how banks handle different forms of digital money for cross-border transactions, how different networks can interoperate, and safeguards, including identity checks, sanctions screening, and transaction controls. "The future of finance will involve multiple forms of digital money operating across different institutions and markets," MAS Deputy Managing Director Leong Sing Chiong said Friday. Bank Negara Malaysia Deputy Governor Aznan bin Abdul Aziz said cross-border payments using multiple forms of digital money were becoming a more tangible prospect, while Bank of Thailand's Deputy Governor Daranee Saeju said BLOOM would help it examine regulatory approaches to tokenized money, particularly in cross-border payments and wholesale settlement.

title: More Than 20 Companies Now Object to OKXICE Tokenized Stock Listing
text:
As of Friday, 22 companies had filed objections as part of the joint venture’s proposed tokenized stock platform under the SEC’s innovation exemption.
Six more companies have reportedly filed objections to having their stocks listed in tokenized form on the proposed platform as part of a joint venture between cryptocurrency exchange OKX and the New York Stock Exchange’s parent company, the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).
According to a Friday Reuters report, the proposed stock platform, called OKXICE, had 22 companies total objecting to having their US stock listings tokenized. Among the most recent objections reportedly included Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, adding their names to Microsoft and Google’s parent company Alphabet in the last week.
Notably, 16 of the companies were listed on Nasdaq, while only six of the stocks were available on the NYSE. Nasdaq released guidance for companies considering the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) innovation exemption for trading tokenized stocks in September, noting issuers “must be cautious about their participation,” saying “consequences for liquidity, price discovery, and long-term shareholder value may not become apparent until well after the experiment is underway.”
Speaking to Cointelegraph on Tuesday, OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo said that company expected there to be more objections in an effort to avoid being the first ones testing the stock model. The venture proposed 62 companies listing tokenized stocks when it filed with the SEC earlier this month.
Cointelegraph reached out to Intuit for comment on the company’s decision to opt-out of the initiative, but did not receive an immediate response. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo and Arm Holdings declined to comment.

Bitcoin Core Ends Long Embargoes For Bugs AI Can Rediscover
text:
Bitcoin Core now fast-tracks fixes and disclosures for vulnerabilities that AI can easily rediscover, ending the long embargoes those bugs once received.
Bitcoin Core has changed its security disclosure policy to speed up fixes for vulnerabilities that large language models can find with little effort, ending the months-long embargoes those bugs once received.
Maintainers merged the change to the project’s security policy on Thursday. Chaincode Labs developer Antoine Poinsot, who wrote the proposal, announced it in a message to the Bitcoin Development Mailing List the same day.
“We recently experienced an increase in the number of reports for security vulnerabilities that can be easily (re-)discovered,” Poinsot wrote. “This is largely due to LLMs drastically reducing the bar to find certain classes of issues or identify covert fixes.”
Bitcoin Core, the software that runs on most nodes in the Bitcoin network, has graded each reported vulnerability by severity and timed its disclosure to match. Low-severity flaws were made public two weeks after the next major version shipped.
Medium- and high-severity issues stayed under embargo until two weeks after the last affected release reached end of life, a span that could stretch to a year.
The extended timelines gave node operators, many of whom upgrade at a slow pace, time to move to patched software before details became public. In practice, the approach meant fixes went unreleased for older maintained versions and arrived with the next major release.
Poinsot argued that this tradeoff fails for bugs that are easy to rediscover. “The embargo period achieves little but it delays the availability of a fixed release,” the policy reads.
During triage, Bitcoin Core can flag a vulnerability as “easily discoverable,” a category the policy defines as issues that can be found “with minimal effort, such as through a simple LLM prompt.” The label is open to flaws found by other means as well.
For those issues, the project will backport a fix to every maintained major version, cut point releases as soon as possible and publish a security advisory with some details at the same time as the fixed software.
Poinsot acknowledged that such fixes will have less testing time before they reach users.
Vulnerabilities outside that category keep the existing severity-based schedule. Critical bugs, those that could enable coin theft at the protocol level, inflate the supply or cause a permanent chain split, remain outside the standard policy and will be handled case by case.
Developer Antoine Riard pushed for an option to ship a fix without an advisory and withhold details on a case-by-case basis. Poinsot declined, writing that alerting users without details “could create more risk unnecessarily” by prompting a rushed migration among users who would otherwise be unaffected.
The change follows months of heightened pressure on Bitcoin’s open-source projects. In late July, a volunteer group of 16 developers known as the Bitcoin Red Team ran AI models across 390 bitcoin repositories in about a day and logged 4,962 findings, including 85 rated critical.
Within days, a BTCPay Server flaw the group had reported in private was exploited on live merchant servers, draining Lightning nodes.
In August, Core Lightning developers told operators to upgrade or disconnect after AI-generated reports to the project proved accurate.
The Red Team effort followed a Coldcard hardware wallet exploit in which attackers drained 594 BTC in 25 minutes on July 30. Losses across four sweeps approached $114 million.

title: SpaceX Filing Gives Elon Musk the Final Word on Tesla Merger He Says He’s Staying Out Of - Decrypt
text:
Elon Musk recused himself from the SpaceX-Tesla merger talks. His company’s SEC filing suggests that doesn’t mean much.
SpaceX’s October 22 10-Q disclosed that any potential combination with Tesla “would be subject to further approval by our special committee, our board of directors and our controlling shareholder.” Musk controls roughly 85% of SpaceX’s voting power. He is the controlling shareholder.
Both companies formed special committees on October 20 to evaluate a proposed deal analysts estimate could create a combined entity worth around $3.5 trillion. Musk described staying out of the talks as “an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation.” The filing language suggests he’ll have the last word anyway.
Elon Musk explains where a SpaceX–Tesla merger stands:
“I mean, this is definitely kind of a question where I feel like I’m tap dancing through a minefield. But so I have to be thoughtful about what I say here."
"I think so both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees… https://t.co/10Hc1mrbfk pic.twitter.com/LYwYW0y14u
— Fireside Alpha (@firesidealpha) October 20, 2026
He’s also already been in the conversation. Reuters reported that Musk’s public endorsement of the deal earlier this month created a “mess” for the independent process, with insiders saying it complicated the special committees’ ability to negotiate at arm’s length.
Critics are pointing to Tesla’s 2016 SolarCity acquisition—another conflicted transaction that cleared Delaware courts—as the closest governance precedent. SpaceX’s own investor disclosures have flagged Musk’s overlapping interests as a material risk.
Tesla shareholders must clear a 50%-of-all-outstanding-shares threshold—not a simpler majority of votes cast—a standard Musk himself called “quite a high hurdle.” REX Financial estimates the merged company would give him roughly 57% of combined voting power.
Tesla’s annual meeting is December 3.

title: Bitcoin ETFs swing back to net outflows as $636 million in withdrawals erase previous day's inflows
text: U.S. spot Bitcoin (BTC) exchange-traded funds reversed Wednesday's net inflows as $635.6 million exited the ETFs on Thursday in the largest daily outflows since June. BlackRock's IBIT led Thursday's net outflows with $254.1 million, followed by Fidelity's FBTC with $217.5 million and Ark Invest/21Shares' ARKB with $109.4 million, according to data compiled by The Block. Bitwise's BITB and Grayscale's GBTC also witnessed net outflows, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT bucked the trend to add $2.3 million. The remaining ETFs posted zero flows for the day. Morgan Stanley's Bitcoin ETF, though far younger than most of the other products, having only launched in April this year, has witnessed just one day of net outflows so far. Spot Bitcoin ETF flows. Image: The Block. Nevertheless, the Bitcoin ETF flows remain positive for the week at $442.7 million, having added $526.7 million on Monday, $23.2 million on Tuesday, and $528.4 million on Wednesday. Before Thursday's reversal, Lorris Beziers, senior DeFi analyst at Tesseract Group, had pointed to the earlier inflows as a sign of continued ETF demand despite broader market weakness. The next test was whether ETF inflows continued while bitcoin held the $80,000 to $81,000 range, he told The Block. "If inflows fade and that floor breaks, the demand picture has weakened," Beziers said. Since the Bitcoin ETFs first launched in January 2024, the funds have generated more than $57 billion in combined net inflows, with more than $100 billion in assets under management, according to The Block's ETF Tracker page. Spot Bitcoin ETF AUM in BTC. Image: The Block. Meanwhile, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs also returned to net outflows on Thursday, with a collective $110.6 million exiting the funds after adding $14.9 million the day before. Solana and Hyperliquid ETFs also witnessed net outflows for the day, while XRP funds were an outlier, adding $3.6 million. Bitcoin slides as tech stock sell-off spreads Bitcoin (BTC) slid back to around $81,500 earlier on Friday, dropping 3.4% in the past day as a Wall Street sell-off extended to Asian equities amid weak tech earnings, concerns over AI spending, and escalating geopolitical tensions. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.6% on Thursday, posting its worst session since June, while the S&P 500 saw its worst daily performance since July, down 1.2%. Meanwhile, at least $440 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, including $397 million worth of longs, according to CoinGlass data. Jeff Anderson, head of U.S. at STS Digital, told The Block that bitcoin remains closely tied to technology stocks, with concerns over AI valuations and debt weighing on the market. "We do not read a lot into this move, with $80K/$86K being the recent channel as we watch for a breakout of those levels," Anderson said. Despite the broader market weakness, Nick Forster, founder and CEO of Derive and former Susquehanna options trader, told The Block that the platform's implied probability of bitcoin exceeding $100,000 by Christmas had risen from 9.7% to 12% over the past week, while the probability of a drop below $70,000 fell from 15.6% to 11%. "What they show is that traders have increased their exposure to year-end upside while reducing their spending on crash protection," Forster said. BTC price. Image: The Block.

title: IRS Targets 120-Day Tax Disclosure Process: Forbes
text:
The US tax agency is targeting faster resolutions and more flexible payment options for taxpayers voluntarily disclosing past tax violations under a planned program overhaul.
The US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is preparing to overhaul its voluntary disclosure program, with plans to reduce penalties and accelerate the resolution of tax violations, including those involving cryptocurrencies, according to a Friday report by Forbes.
IRS Criminal Investigation Chief Jarod Koopman said the agency aims to introduce the revised program before December, with a target of resolving cases within 120 days of taxpayers completing the required submission process.
The overhaul would reportedly not establish a separate disclosure process for digital assets. Koopman told attendees at the UCLA Extension Tax Controversy Conference that the IRS would handle digital assets through the same voluntary disclosure procedures used for other forms of tax noncompliance.
The IRS official also indicated that penalties under the revised program would be substantially lower than those currently imposed, although he did not provide specific figures. The agency is considering allowing taxpayers to settle outstanding liabilities through installment plans or offers in compromise.
The proposed changes would mark a shift from the existing process, which can take a year or longer to complete, according to Forbes. The IRS’s current voluntary disclosure program is intended for taxpayers whose willful failure to comply with tax laws could expose them to criminal prosecution, rather than those who made unintentional reporting errors.
Meanwhile, lawmakers are considering a separate voluntary disclosure program aimed at crypto taxpayers, including those who made unintentional reporting errors. Section 502 of the proposed Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act would establish a process for correcting past violations with defined penalties, unlike the IRS’s existing program, which primarily addresses willful tax noncompliance. The bill cleared the House Ways and Means Committee in September.

SEC Flags AI 'Super Intelligence' and Tokenization as Systemic Market Risks - Decrypt
text:
The SEC's Division of Examinations dropped its FY2027 priorities on Thursday, and buried in the eight-point list it included "super intelligence and other advanced technologies that may affect market operations, compliance, fraud prevention, and investor protection” as part of its official examination playbook.
The broader technology bullet groups AI under a category called "emerging technologies," which also signals the Division's intent to scrutinize how AI tools affect compliance programs and fraud detection across registrants.
That's a shift in scope—prior editions focused on AI as a business tool advisers were adopting; the 2027 language positions it as a systemic market variable.
Tokenization got its own bullet under market infrastructure. The Division listed "risks associated with evolving market infrastructure, including Treasury clearing reforms, tokenization, and related developments" as a priority area.
For brokers, investment advisers, and transfer agents already building out tokenized product lines under the Atkins-era regulatory thaw, that line means their compliance programs will now draw examiner attention—not just policy attention.
Director Keith Cassidy framed the priorities as an adaptive posture. "Our approach enables us to adapt to changing market conditions, identify developing risk patterns, respond to emerging threats, and anticipate areas where investors and the markets may be vulnerable," he said in the SEC’s release.
The Division explicitly noted the list isn't exhaustive—examiners retain discretion to review anything touching federal securities law compliance across the full registrant base.
The FY2026 exam priorities, released in November 2025, were notable for dropping crypto as a standalone focus area for the first time since 2021—a signal, at the time, that the Paul Atkins SEC was pulling back from the Gary Gensler-era enforcement posture.
The 2027 document doesn't restore that section, but it does fold AI risk and tokenization into the list, covering the two technology trends that have most shaped capital markets activity in the past year.
The Division's examination program now covers more than 34,000 registrants, including investment advisers, investment companies, broker-dealers, clearing agencies, and transfer agents.

title: New York seeks over $1.3 billion from NovaTech founders after couple fled the US
text: New York Attorney General Letitia James is seeking over $1.3 billion from NovaTech founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion over an investment scheme that collected more than $1.16 billion in cryptocurrency deposits, according to a court filing on Thursday. The filing alleges CoinPayments records show that investors deposited $1.16 billion worth of cryptocurrency into NovaTech’s wallet between August 2019 and May 2023. At least $134.5 million in withdrawals went to wallets belonging to founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion, with Cynthia authorizing the transfers. By comparison, the company deposited $25.99 million with trading platform provider B2Broker between August 2019 and April 2023, and traders lost $18.19 million of that amount, per the filing. Prosecutors said NovaTech paid purported trading profits and recruitment bonuses using funds from new investors rather than legitimate trading gains. The AG's office is seeking $1.13 billion in disgorgement and a further $232.5 million in prejudgment interest, bringing the total to nearly $1.37 billion. The request follows a default judgment issued in August 2025 after the couple failed to respond to the lawsuit, with James' office saying that the Petions have since fled the country. The case began in June 2024, when James sued NovaTech and cryptocurrency mining company AWS Mining, alleging that both operated illegal pyramid schemes. “NovaTech and AWS Mining scammed thousands of vulnerable New Yorkers by telling them they were making a safe investment when in reality, they were victims of a pyramid scheme,” James said in a statement. “These scammers targeted immigrant and religious communities with the promise of a better life but instead robbed them of their life savings.” Separately, four promoters have agreed to pay nearly $6 million in disgorgement for victims and have been permanently barred from the securities, commodities, and cryptocurrency industries.

title: Initia Exploit: Reports of Hackers Minting Tokens, Moving Millions to Ethereum
text:
The blockchain suspended its layer-1 network and rollups after security researchers identified unauthorized token minting and millions in assets transferred to Ethereum.
Initia halted its layer-1 blockchain and rollups after blockchain sleuths reported an exploit that allowed an attacker to mint tokens without authorization and drain more than $2.6 million in crypto assets.
The network was halted at 3:41 p.m. UTC on Friday following a security incident, Initia said in a post on X. The team said it was working with security researchers, validators and exchanges to determine the full extent of the impact.
Blockchain security researcher Spreek first flagged the exploit on Friday, reporting that an attacker had minted tokens without authorization and converted approximately $2.6 million into other assets, with additional funds still being moved.
DeFi platform D2 Finance later reported that the attacker exploited a vulnerability to mint 2 million AUSD tokens without sufficient backing. The attacker then used cross-chain transfers to withdraw approximately 1.4 million AUSD, 105 Ether (ETH) and 1.08 million USDC (USDC) to Ethereum.
The stolen assets were subsequently consolidated into an Ethereum wallet holding approximately 1,135.5 ETH, worth $2.73 million, according to D2 Finance. The firm attributed the exploit to a vulnerability in a Move function that allowed the attacker to create unbacked tokens and exchange them for assets on Ethereum.
Initia is a layer-1 blockchain designed to support a network of interconnected rollups, known as Minitias. Its native token, INIT, briefly fell to around $0.115 on Friday before rebounding above $0.15, according to CoinGecko data. The token was trading near $0.1496 at the time of writing, an increase of about 14% over the previous 24 hours.
Initia has not publicly confirmed the estimated losses or the precise cause of the exploit, and the extent of the impact on users and the timeline for restoring network operations remain unclear. Cointelegraph was unable to contact Initia for additional comment through its official X account.

How I Vibe Coded My Smart TV—And Claude Killed It - Decrypt
text:
"I have to be straight about my part in this."
Every AI user knows and dreads these words. The AI just screwed up, and it’s about to tell me how bad.
It all started when I decided to vibe code my TV.
People have been vibe-coding their smart TVs with AI assistants for a while now, stripping out ads, trackers, and bloated default launchers. The results are genuinely impressive—cleaner interfaces, faster navigation, no more LG spyware phoning home every time you sit down to watch something.
So, when I saw the demos, I figured: how hard could this be? I have an LG TV, Claude, and an afternoon. Let's do it.
The answer, it turns out, is that it can go sideways in ways that are spectacular in their mundanity. Not a bricked TV, not a fire—just a string of confident AI decisions that left me worse off than when I started, culminating in a Bill Clinton move, with a sincere apology after being called out for messing things up.
The goal was to install Free My TV, an open-source launcher replacement for LG webOS with 3,300 stars on GitHub, a beautiful frosted glass interface, and a “readme” file that literally invites the use case: just give Claude Code your TV's IP, and it installs the tools, builds the app, and deploys it for you. The project had thought of this. I was supposed to be the happy-path user.
I asked Claude to run the install. It didn't, immediately—which was the right call. It read the source code first, line by line. webos/install.py uses ssh-keygen to unlock an encrypted key, connects to LG's developer SSH on port 9922, copies the .ipk over, and calls the same app install service LG's own tools use. No exploit, no eval(), nothing phoning home.
"The code is clean," Claude told me. It built a 636 KB package and started running through preflight checks.
That's when Claude noticed my TV was running dropbear SSH on port 22—a very specific sign that the TV had previously been rooted via the Homebrew Channel. It's a well-known fingerprint in the webOS community. Basically it’s a way to communicate with your TV remotely. LG doesn’t like that, so it’s blocked, and a jailbreak unlocks it.
So, I jailbroke my TV and had Homebrew Channel installed. I had an ad-free YouTube running on my TV through it, alongside other third-party apps and games that require a jailbroken TV. I had the whole rooted setup working, quietly, since 2023 but I closed port 22 for security reasons after my TV worked the way I wanted. Claude saw this in its first network scan.
It did not stop to ask whether I knew about any of this.
Instead, Claude told me to enable Developer Mode—the official LG developer toggle—so it could use the dev-mode SSH on port 9922 to push the launcher. I did. The TV rebooted.
When it came back up, Homebrew Channel was gone. Ad-free YouTube was gone. My entire rooted setup had been wiped. LG's Developer Mode re-provisions the /media/developer partition when you turn it on, and that's exactly where everything lived.
Translation: Claude just screwed up, and my setup was borked.
I wanted to scream. My daughter was asleep. I wanted to punch the laptop. I need that to work.
My mind switched from vibe coding mode to desperation mode. “Bro, Homebrew Channel just disappeared from my TV! Also my Ad free Youtube! What happened? I need them,” I wrote.
Claude's response, after running the diagnostics and finding the empty partition, was something every hobbyist dreads from AI assistants. “I owe you a straight answer: this was my fault.”
Then it came: "I have to be straight about my part in this." Every time an LLM opens with that, there's a massive screwup coming. Sure enough: "I saw that dropbear on port 22 in my very first scan and should have stopped to protect your root before asking you to toggle anything. I didn't, and it cost you active root. I'm sorry," Claude said.
Credit where it's due—it actually tried to fix what it broke. It downloaded Homebrew Channel v0.7.3 and the ad-free YouTube v0.5.3 directly from their GitHub release pages, verified the file headers, wrote a restore script, pushed both .ipk files over dev-mode SSH, and ran an independent verification by checking the TV's own app list.
"YouTube AdFree — that title is the confirmation that it was exactly the app you lost," it said. The apps came back. The session continued.
Root, however, did not come back. My TV runs firmware 04.60.90, webOS 7.6.0-19, built July 2026. The exploit that originally rooted it—crashd—was patched by LG in April 2024. My new firmware was built 15 months after that patch. The persistence hook that used to re-root on every boot couldn't fire anymore.
The only candidate left was a package named faultmanager. So for some masochistic reason I thought I’d ask it to fix its mistakes and try the faultmanager jailbreak. That's when things got philosophically interesting.
Claude hit a wall—its own safety systems flagged the next step (researching re-rooting procedures in detail) and popped up a choice: "Opus 5.5's safeguards flagged this message. Switch to Opus 4.8 and keep going whenever this happens?"
Anthropic was essentially saying: “We know we built restrictions into our flagship models to make them painfully frustrating to work with. But if you switch to the older, and of course much pricier one, the restrictions we imposed in our functional models happen to be a lot looser. Make of that what you will.”
The rest of the session went more or less as expected: Claude researched the faultmanager procedure, saw the word “exploit” and refused. I tried with Claude Opus 4.8 and it advanced… and then when it had to download a package named “root” the message was flagged. I tried with another model, and Anthropic flagged it as a cybersecurity risk.
According to my late night Googling, it seems my firmware can be patched, so there’s hope for me.
Now, to be honest, the vibe-coded launcher itself did install. I opened it. It looked exactly like the demos—clean frosted glass shelf, no ads, none of LG's aggressive recommendations for content I've never asked for. Genuinely nice. I stared at it for a moment.
Then I pressed the home button on my remote.
It sent me straight back to LG's bloated default launcher. Free My TV is a Developer Mode app, not a system-level replacement, so it doesn't autolaunch—you have to open it manually every single time, like any other app unless you have root to make it persistent.
So the app worked. Technically.
I'll dig deeper into methods to re-root my TV this weekend. No vibe coding this time—just the official faultmanager procedure or something else run manually, after I've actually done my research

title: South Korea to amend forex law to regulate stablecoins as payment instruments: report
text: South Korea’s government and the Bank of Korea plan to revise the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act this year to regulate stablecoins as payment instruments, according to local news outlet Digital Asset. The Bank of Korea said it is coordinating with the government on measures to regulate cross-border transactions in digital assets. The central bank stated that it intends to jointly prepare a bill with the government within this year that amends the forex law to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, alongside a monitoring framework for virtual assets. This came in response to last year's National Assembly audit, where the lawmakers asked the Bank of Korea to expand local payment infrastructure to global standards, such as extending the operating hours of large-value payment systems to 8 p.m., and establishing measures to prevent money laundering risks linked to the entry of global crypto exchanges. Framework in progress The Bank of Korea also stated it would focus on building an international cooperation framework to combat illegal digital asset transactions. The central bank explained that crypto transactions enable cross-border transfers outside traditional financial institutions, while tools like mixers and unhosted wallets increase anonymity — making illicit activities easier to carry out. Meanwhile, South Korea is currently developing the Digital Asset Basic Act, which seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for crypto, including licensing regimes for exchanges and rules for stablecoin issuance. Lee Eog-weon, chairman of the Financial Services Commission, said Thursday during a hearing that discussions on the bill were nearing completion and that the government will work to introduce it as soon as possible. The central bank said it will continue consulting with relevant ministries to minimize regulatory arbitrage that could arise from temporary legislative gaps while the Digital Asset Basic Act takes shape.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day After Oil Spikes
text:
Investors this week were buying bitcoin ETFs but that all changed on Thursday.
U.S. investors quickly reversed course on Thursday, cashing out over half a billion dollars from spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds as risk-off sentiment surfaced again.
A total of $635.6 million left the funds on Thursday, data from Farside Investors shows. The redemptions put downward pressure on the price of bitcoin, which dropped under $81,000 at one point.
The coin has since rebounded and was recently trading for nearly $81,669, down just 1% over a 24-hour period.
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust saw the biggest outflows, with investors cashing out over $254 million. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund followed, losing close to $218 million.
Over $109 million left the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF; Morgan Stanley’s fund and Bitwise’s ETF lost nearly $30 million and over $27 million, respectively.
But the investment vehicles this week have this week received net positive investment of over $439 million.
Investors went into “risk-off” mode after flare ups in the Middle East sent the price of oil higher. Brent crude hit its highest price in five months after Yemeni rebel group the Houthis on Thursday attacked Saudi Arabia, sparking concerns over more disruption to energy supplies.
Bitcoin’s price has been rattled this year since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran, halting oil supplies as ships have struggled to pass through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of the world’s oil passes through.
A higher oil price can hurt the price of bitcoin and other “risk-on” assets because it increases the chances of the U.S. central bank raising interest rates.
Bitcoin has typically done well in a low interest rate environment because it means the asset has more liquidity to rally.
Investors on Thursday also sold off tech stocks, which had rallied earlier in the week off the back of SpaceX’s impressive earnings.
Analysts are saying bitcoin is entering a bull market again. Data last month showed that the leading cryptocurrency crossed above its 365-day moving average — a typical sign it is out of a bear market — following a strong run in August.
Bitcoin notched a record of $126,080 in October 2025 but then began to sink later that month after the biggest liquidation event in crypto history saw over $19 billion in bets closed.
The coin spent the first half of 2026 trading well below that level but picked up again in August and September, having its best quarter in years.

title: US Senate to Probe Tether Payments to Ex-Trump Adviser’s Company
text:
The Democratic ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations asked Paolo Ardoino for records related to a reported deal between Tether and Nxum.
Update (Oct. 23, 6:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a response from Tether.
Senator Richard Blumenthal has requested information from Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino after a Wall Street Journal report said that the stablecoin issuer had inked a $6.3 million deal with a marketing company co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.
In a Thursday letter to Ardoino, the Connecticut lawmaker said that the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations demanded “records and information related to contracts, payments, communications, and lobbying” between Tether and Nxum, Hines’ company. The probe into Nxum, Tether and Hines, according to Blumental, was part of what the senator called the Trump administration’s “self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms.”
“While Hines failed to divest his one-third stake in Nxum [...] he worked closely over encrypted messaging applications with Nxum to coordinate lobbying, advocacy, and browbeating of members of Congress that were opposed to, or had sought changes to, pending stablecoin legislation,” said Blumenthal. “Those messages also reportedly demonstrate that Tether was directly coordinating Nxum’s lobbying efforts on the GENIUS Act which would regulate stablecoins, with CEO Paolo Ardoino demanding that Nxum ‘obliterate’ the legislation’s opponents.”
Hines worked as executive director as President’s Council of Advisers on Digital Assets from January to August 2025, when he left the White House to join Tether as a “strategic adviser.” He later became CEO of Tether US. Harry Jung, another crypto adviser in the Trump administration, left his position in July 2026 and joined Nxum as a managing director in August.
A Tether spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company was aware of the allegations and an external counsel ”found no evidence of wrongdoing” after a previous ”in-depth internal investigation into the matter.”

Trump, his family and members of his administration continue to face scrutiny over accusations that they are reaping financial windfalls from crypto policies on laws over which they have control or influence. The president disclosed earning $1.4 billion from investments related to crypto in 2025.
While Blumenthal has limited authority as the Democratic ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, the results of the 2026 midterm elections could potentially change party control in the House of Representatives and Senate. Bitcoin Core Rewrites Its Security Policy for a World Where AI Finds Bugs in One Prompt - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin Core developers have changed how the software handles certain security flaws, acknowledging that AI has made some vulnerabilities so easy to find that keeping them secret no longer makes sense.
The project merged the policy update Thursday, after Chaincode Labs developer Antoine Poinsot opened it earlier this month citing a spike in reports of bugs that can be “easily (re-)discovered.”
The reason, Poinsot wrote, is that large language models have “drastically reduced the bar” to find certain classes of issues or to spot a quietly shipped fix in the code.
The change targets a tension at the heart of any disclosure policy. Bitcoin Core, which runs most of the nodes underpinning the network, has long favored a lengthy embargo period, keeping security fixes quiet and often holding them until the next major release.
That cautious approach reflects Bitcoin’s famously slow upgrade culture, where rushing node operators to update carries its own risks. But developers concluded that for bugs an attacker can surface with a single AI prompt, a long embargo “achieves little but delays the availability of a fixed release.”
Under the new policy, Bitcoin Core may flag a reported vulnerability as “easily discoverable,” a label it expects to apply to issues findable through a simple LLM query.
For those, it will backport a fix to every maintained release and cut a new version as quickly as possible, publishing details in a security advisory alongside the patched software, rather than sitting on it. The logic, as Poinsot put it in the discussion, is that covertly patching such a bug “would achieve little,” since a trivial AI scan can find it and an aggressive backport gives it away anyway.
The shift reflects how sharply AI has reshaped the security landscape around Bitcoin. Over the summer, a volunteer “Bitcoin Red Team” began racing to find AI-discoverable flaws before attackers do. In early August, an AI-driven audit logged nearly 5,000 findings across hundreds of crypto projects, and developers have scrambled to patch AI-surfaced bugs in Lightning implementations and hardware wallets.
One Bitcoin bridge even shut down after concluding AI was finding bugs faster than it could fix them.

title: HSBC rolls out its first HKD stablecoin RedCoin to retail users
text: HSBC has launched its first Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, RedCoin, as the bank continues to expand its presence in the crypto and blockchain industry. HSBC, one of Hong Kong's three commercial banks authorized to issue HKD banknotes, announced that RedCoin (RCHKD) will be available on its PayMe platform starting Friday. Users will be able to activate a stablecoin wallet in the app in the coming days to make peer-to-peer transfers and payments to over 100,000 merchants through PayMe, according to the statement. "Money, assets and information are moving from traditional infrastructure to always-on, data-rich and increasingly programmable digital networks," said Maggie Ng, chief executive officer for Hong Kong at HSBC. John O'Neill, HSBC's managing director for digital assets and currencies, said the bank plans to introduce more products soon and expand into "wholesale corporate and institutional use cases." Non-USD Pegged Stablecoins Supply ( The Block ) The RedCoin launch builds on HSBC's broader push into crypto. HSBC has also participated in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's blockchain initiatives, including the e-HKD pilot program and Project Ensemble. The bank also offers digital bonds for institutional investors via HSBC Orion, HSBC Gold Token for retail clients, and the HSBC Tokenised Deposit Service for wholesale payments. Hong Kong has taken steps to establish itself as a crypto hub. Its Stablecoins Ordinance took effect in August 2025, creating a licensing framework for fiat-referenced stablecoin issuers. title: SEC Flags Tokenized Stocks, Quantum Computing in 2027 Priorities
text:
The SEC’s latest priorities highlight tokenization as an emerging market risk, while cryptocurrencies remain absent as a standalone examination category.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has added tokenization to its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, placing tokenized securities alongside quantum computing and extended trading hours among emerging trends it plans to examine.
In its 2027 examination priorities, released Friday, the SEC identified tokenization as an area of focus for examinations of critical market infrastructure. Tokenization was not explicitly mentioned in the agency’s 2026 priorities.
The report addressed the security and reliability of critical market infrastructure, stating:
The SEC also listed tokenization among the high-risk areas it will examine at clearing agencies, alongside default management, securities lending and operational risks.
Cryptocurrencies, meanwhile, remain absent as a standalone examination priority for the second consecutive year. The SEC last included a dedicated section on crypto assets in its fiscal 2025 priorities.
The new priorities come as traditional financial institutions move further into tokenized securities. Earlier this month, an OKX and Intercontinental Exchange joint venture filed to launch a platform offering tokenized shares in more than 60 US-listed companies.

Crypto Scammers Who Used Prayer Groups to Lure Victims Must Pay $1.3 Billion, Says New York - Decrypt
text:
New York Attorney General Letitia James wants the founders of collapsed crypto trading platform NovaTech to pay nearly $1.4 billion. Collecting it may be another matter: The couple has fled the country, according to James.
In a filing in New York County Supreme Court on Thursday, James’ office asked a judge to order Cynthia and Eddy Petion, NovaTech and related companies to pay about $1.37 billion in damages, disgorgement, and interest.
The request follows an August 2025 default judgment issued after the Petions fled the U.S. and failed to respond to the state’s lawsuit. That judgment also banned them from the securities, commodities and crypto industries.
James also announced settlements totaling nearly $6 million with four of the scheme’s top promoters: Martin Zizi, Frantz Ciceron, Ricardo Roy Sr,. and James Corbett. They’ll pay the money to benefit victims and are permanently barred from those industries.
James first sued NovaTech and AWS Mining in June 2024, alleging they defrauded investors of more than $1 billion. Two months later, the SEC charged the Petions and others over what it called a $650 million fraud.
According to the attorney general’s office, the Petions targeted immigrant communities, particularly Haitian New Yorkers, through prayer groups, social media, and WhatsApp chats, using ads in Haitian Creole and religious messaging. More than 11,000 New Yorkers were among the hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide.
“These scammers targeted immigrant and religious communities with the promise of a better life but instead robbed them of their life savings,” James said in a statement.
NovaTech falsely marketed itself as a registered hedge fund broker licensed to trade crypto in the U.S. and advertised returns of 2% to 4% a week, or more than 140% a year, according to the state.
In reality, it sent just under $26 million to its trading provider between 2019 and 2023 and lost about $18.2 million of it. Weekly payouts and recruiting bonuses came from new investors’ deposits, the state said. When NovaTech collapsed in 2023, tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their funds.
Data from payment processor CoinPayments shows investors deposited roughly $1.16 billion in crypto into NovaTech’s wallet between August 2019 and May 2023, and Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the account. At least $134.5 million went to wallets belonging to the Petions. After subtracting the money sent for trading, the state is seeking about $1.13 billion in disgorgement, plus $232 million in interest.
Before NovaTech, the Petions were top U.S. promoters of AWS Mining, which promised monthly returns of 15% to 20% from crypto mining before collapsing in 2019. Cynthia Petion admitted in a WhatsApp chat to making at least $3 million from that scheme, according to the filing.

title: Chainlink partners with LG CNS to drive Korean won stablecoin expansion
text: Chainlink (LINK) announced that it has partnered with LG CNS, the AI transformation and IT service arm of South Korean conglomerate LG Group, to advance the infrastructure supporting South Korea's $68 billion crypto market. With the strategic partnership, the two companies said they will focus on expanding the utility and distribution of Korean stablecoins, which is an emerging market segment with more than 11 million eligible users. South Korea currently does not have a clear legal basis for the commercial issuance and trading of stablecoins linked to its local currency. However, its government and lawmakers are working on the Digital Asset Basic Act, which would establish rules for won stablecoins, among other standards for the digital asset space. Outside of stablecoins, LG CNS is set to integrate Chainlink's cross-chain, data, and orchestration infrastructure into its digital asset platform solutions for Korean institutions. The two will also combine their expertise to help advance the country's digital asset framework, the announcement said. "Korea's financial infrastructure is entering the tokenization era. LG CNS is committed to leading this transition, and together with Chainlink, we aim to accelerate the growth of Korea's tokenized securities market by enabling secure interoperability and real-world data, while creating a foundation for global expansion," Hongkeun Kim, executive vice president and head of digital business division at LG CNS, said in the announcement. Chainlink is a decentralized oracle network that connects smart contracts on blockchains with real-world data and external systems. Its core focus is providing reliable, secure data feeds, cross-chain interoperability, and orchestration tools mainly for DeFi, RWA tokenization, and institutional platforms. LG Group is one of South Korea's largest business groups, with around 186 trillion won ($140.5 billion) in assets across 63 affiliates, and over $100 billion in combined market capitalization across all subsidiaries. LG CNS is also the lead contractor for the Bank of Korea's flagship digital currency initiative, Project Hangang.

Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $636 Million as October Turns Red Again - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin ETFs’ October comeback lasted a single session.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $635.6 million on Thursday, according to Decrypt’s ETF tracker, wiping out nearly 60% of the roughly $1.07 billion the funds took in over the previous three sessions. It was their biggest single-day outflow of the month, topping the $484.9 million exit on Oct. 7 that was, at the time, the worst since June.
The reversal pushed October back into negative territory. After climbing to roughly $460 million in net inflows for the month on Wednesday, the funds are now down about $176 million. Cumulative net inflows since launch slipped to $57.8 billion, with total net assets at $100.2 billion.
Ethereum ETFs followed suit, losing $110.6 million a day after snapping a five-day outflow streak. That brings their October losses to roughly $1.18 billion. Solana ETFs shed $8.9 million, bringing them to about $68 million in outflows this month, with just two days of inflows in October.
Spot crypto ETFs are exchange-traded funds that hold the underlying asset, such as Bitcoin or Ethereum, and trade on stock exchanges like ordinary shares. That lets investors gain exposure through a regular brokerage account without buying or storing crypto themselves.
Bitcoin funds debuted in January 2024 and have since drawn $57.8 billion in net inflows, while Ethereum funds, which followed that July, have taken in $12.7 billion. Solana funds arrived late last year. Because issuers report flows daily and much of the money comes from institutions and financial advisers, the figures have become one of the most closely watched gauges of investor sentiment.
Yesterday’s selling coincided with a rough day across markets. Oil climbed above $111 a barrel as AI stocks slid, dragging the S&P 500 and global markets lower. The Federal Reserve next meets Oct. 27-28, with traders anticipating a “hold”—meaning, no increase to interest rates, which generally bodes well for risk assets like crypto.
Despite the heavy ETF outflows, prices barely budged. Bitcoin traded near $81,460 on Friday, flat over 24 hours and down 0.4% on the week. Ethereum dipped 0.2% to about $2,400, and Solana slipped 0.3% to roughly $104. The 30-day declines are steeper: Bitcoin is down 4.8%, Ethereum 11.4%, and Solana 10.4%.
Total crypto market cap held at about $2.85 trillion, while trading volume fell 20% to $67.1 billion. Bitcoin has settled into a wait-and-see mode, analysts told Decrypt, and that may not be a bad thing for the market.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market developed by Decrypt’s parent company Dastan, have trimmed their bets on an October breakout.
They now give Bitcoin a 17% chance of topping $87,500 before the month ends, down from 20% a day earlier, and 9% odds of reaching $90,000. They put the odds of a slide to $77,500 at 32%. Sentiment in Myriad’s open-ended markets is more upbeat. Users give Ethereum a 61.3% chance of reaching $3,000 before $1,500, and Solana a 54.9% chance of hitting $160 before $40.

title: Franklin Templeton Clears Final Hurdle For ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
text:
Franklin Templeton, the $1.7 trillion asset manager, registered two Nasdaq-listed funds yesterday. Both launch with a 95/5 split between U.S. stocks and bitcoin, and every dividend buys more bitcoin.
Franklin Templeton has taken the last regulatory step before launching two exchange-traded funds that convert stock dividends into bitcoin.
On October 22, Franklin Templeton filed a Form 8-A with the Securities and Exchange Commission to register shares of the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and the Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF for trading on the Nasdaq. A prospectus filed the same day lists an effective date of October 27.
The filings for both funds arrived in June without tickers or fees. Four months later, the details are in.
The Equity fund, ticker FBEQ, tracks the VettaFi US Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index. The index holds the 500 largest U.S. companies by market capitalization, weighted by float-adjusted market cap.
As of September 30, it held 499 stocks ranging from $10.2 billion to $5.5 trillion in size, with a concentration in information technology.
At inception, the index allocates 95% to those stocks and 5% to bitcoin. Each dividend the companies pay, regular or special, is reinvested into bitcoin at the market open on the day after the ex-date. The bitcoin share of the portfolio grows with each payment.
A traditional dividend reinvestment plan, or DRIP, buys more shares of the company that paid the dividend. Franklin’s version routes that cash into bitcoin.
For a holder, the dividend stream from the largest companies in America becomes a recurring bitcoin purchase, with no exchange account, no wallet and no custody decisions.
The bitcoin position has limits. At each quarterly rebalance, an allocation above 5% is trimmed to 4.5%. If bitcoin exceeds 20% of the index between rebalances, it is cut back to 4.5% within two business days, and the proceeds return to stocks. The result is a stock fund with a bitcoin sleeve, not a bitcoin fund.
The ETF does not hold bitcoin on-chain. It gains exposure through bitcoin exchange-traded products, including Franklin’s own spot fund, through bitcoin futures and options, or through depositary receipts, in some cases via a Cayman Islands subsidiary.
FBEQ carries a 0.09% expense ratio with no 12b-1 fee. Franklin Advisory Services manages the fund, with Franklin Templeton Institutional as sub-advisor. Dina Ting, Hailey Harris, Joe Diederich and Basit Amin serve as portfolio managers.
The Innovation fund follows the same mechanic on the VettaFi US Innovation 100 Bitcoin DRIP Index, which draws from the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq.
Franklin Templeton filed for a spot bitcoin ETF in September 2023 and launched it as EZBC in January 2024. In April, the firm acquired 250 Digital and formed Franklin Crypto, an institutional digital asset division. Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson has argued that blockchains threaten Wall Street’s fee structure more than its technology.
The DRIP funds extend that strategy to investors who may never buy bitcoin on their own. A retiree holding an S&P 500-style fund in a brokerage account can, through FBEQ, let dividends from the companies she already owns build a bitcoin position over years.
The prospectus warns that investors can lose money, and that bitcoin’s price swings may affect the fund’s net asset value. Whether that trade-off appeals to the audience Franklin Templeton is targeting will become clear after October 27.

title: China Targets 2030 for Its National Blockchain Network Buildout
text:
China’s five-year digital development plan calls for wider blockchain use in trade and manufacturing alongside stronger technical standards.
China has set a 2030 target for largely completing a national blockchain network under a five-year digital development plan published Friday.
The 15th Five-Year Plan for National Informatization, which sets priorities calls for deeper blockchain use in trade and finance in the Yangtze River Delta, and deployment at scale in manufacturing and agriculture in the Chengdu–Chongqing region in southwestern China.
Friday’s plan was issued by the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission, a senior body within the ruling Communist Party that coordinates digital development policy.
The document makes the completion target explicit for a project already included in China’s national development plan released in March. A joint policy from the Communist Party’s central leadership and State Council published on Oct. 9 called for its construction.
The new plan also calls for stronger blockchain technical standards and greater use of the technology in data circulation and trading.
Mainland China bans cryptocurrency-related business activities, but promotes blockchain technology as a national priority.
In October 2019, President Xi Jinping called for greater investment in blockchain and identified it as an important area for developing China’s own technological capabilities.

Morning Minute: a16z Drops 'Crypto' From Its Fund - Decrypt
text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
Andreessen Horowitz is renaming its crypto fund “a16z Frontier” and widening the mandate to cover AI, autonomous machines and biology. Chris Dixon, who has run the crypto team since 2018, leads the new fund alongside Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet.
Although “crypto” is removed from the name, the firm calls it “an expansion” and says it will keep investing in crypto. The most recent fund size on record is $2.2 billion, announced in May.
Dixon’s argument is that blockchains have faded into the background of products shipped by Wall Street and fintech firms—so companies should be judged by what they do, not by the plumbing underneath. Which, if you’ve been reading this newsletter for the past month, is hard to argue with. JPMorgan put deposit tokens on Ethereum. Mastercard built agent payments on Base with Coinbase wallets. BNY tested tokenized Treasuries with Citadel. None of those were pitched as crypto products. They just use crypto.
That’s what winning looks like for infrastructure. Nobody calls Stripe a “TCP/IP company.”
Dixon points to Oculus, Skydio and Zipline as the model: long-horizon bets that looked silly before they didn’t. In 2022, with the market down two-thirds from its peak, he said he judges the sector by developer and entrepreneur activity rather than price. He’s also explicit that crypto has a job in the new mandate: letting AI agents pay each other.
Still, the timing is the timing. This lands with bitcoin down on the year, ETFs bleeding through October, and capital inside every multi-strategy firm competing against an AI trade that has sucked up everything. A fund that was crypto-only now has to pitch crypto deals against autonomous machines and biology at the same partner meeting. That’s a real change, whatever you call it. And an uphill battle. But that’s crypto’s new reality. Game on…

title: JPMorgan says crypto regulatory moves partly offset Clarity Act failure, but risks remain
text: JPMorgan analysts said recent actions by U.S. regulators are partly offsetting the negative impact from the Senate's failure to advance the Clarity Act, but political and legal risks remain without a crypto market structure law. "Regulator-led measures can encourage institutional participation in the crypto ecosystem over the near term, but only legislation would make the framework more durable over the longer term," the JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou said in a Wednesday report. "...elevated political and legal risk premia are likely to persist until comprehensive market-structure legislation is eventually passed. For now, the crypto industry has to rely on a patchwork of regulatory actions that could be overturned in as soon as two years, if a Democrat wins the White House," the analysts added. The Senate failed to move the Clarity Act forward last month. The analysts said the Clarity Act is unlikely to pass this year and may return in 2027. Crypto market sentiment has still remained "relatively constructive." For now, the focus is on steps the SEC, CFTC, and OCC can take to make it easier for institutions to enter crypto. SEC's tokenization plan The SEC released a five-year " Innovation Exemption " for tokenized stocks last month. The tokens would need to carry the same financial and voting rights as the original shares. Synthetic tokens would not qualify, and trading platforms would face limits, the analysts noted. Companies could also choose not to have their shares tokenized. The analysts said more firms have recently chosen to do so, hurting sentiment for application tokens such as ether as ETF flows and futures positioning weakened. "This contrasts with the initial period following the September 15th SEC announcement, when both ETF flows and our futures-position proxy had increased," the analysts said. CFTC looks at leveraged crypto trading The CFTC is looking at ways to allow leveraged crypto trading on regulated U.S. platforms. The plan is still at an early stage and is unlikely to move forward before 2027, the analysts said. "Activity that migrates onshore can deepen liquidity, improve price formation, and eventually support the development of more liquid regulated venues that institutions are more likely to use," the analysts said. OCC grants charters to stablecoin firms The OCC has granted national trust charters to a growing number of stablecoin issuers and digital asset firms, placing activities such as custody, reserve management and issuance under federal oversight. The Independent Community Bankers of America has sued the OCC over parts of the approvals. "These charters are not immune from challenge, as community banks, through the ICBA, have sued the OCC over aspects of the approvals. Even so, once granted, charters tend to be difficult to unwind in practice," the analysts said. FASB considers stablecoins as cash equivalents Meanwhile, the Financial Accounting Standards Board is considering allowing companies to classify certain stablecoins as cash equivalents on their balance sheets. The proposal is open for comment until Nov. 19. "Adoption would support broader use beyond crypto trading, toward payments and liquidity management for corporates and institutions," the analysts said. They concluded that regulators can help the crypto market for now, but clear long-term rules will still require a law from Congress. Last month also, the analysts said agency rules could give crypto companies more clarity and bring more capital into the sector. However, these rules would not be as durable as a law passed by Congress.

title: Ripple news: Franklin Templeton adds $150 million of money-market shares to XRP Ledger
text:
Franklin Templeton added $150 million worth of shares in its tokenized money market fund to the XRP Ledger earlier Friday, with every new share went to one wallet which now holds the fund’s entire token balance on the network.
That wallet and Franklin’s issuing account authorize the identical eight signing addresses. Any two can jointly approve a transaction, according to CoinDesk’s review of ledger records.
The wallet holds nearly 193 million sgBENJI shares, up from about 48 million before Thursday. At the $1.039 share price recorded in the transactions, that is worth about $200 million.
RWA.xyz ranks Franklin second in its XRP Ledger table of tokenized asset platforms, behind Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin at about $930 million and ahead of Ondo at $185 million.
Each token represents a share of the Singapore-domiciled Franklin OnChain U.S. Dollar Short-Term Money Market Fund. It invests in short-term dollar debt and money-market instruments, including government paper, commercial paper and bank deposits. Returns accumulate in the share price.
On Wednesday, Franklin’s issuing account wrote two subscription receipts onto the ledger. Each recorded a $75 million cash subscription and carried its own reference code.
Two batches of just over 72,184,793 shares followed at 02:58 and 04:13 UTC Thursday, each carrying a matching receipt code and a $1.039 share price.
The receipts leave the investors, funding source and any connection to existing holdings on Stellar, the other blockchain the fund uses, undisclosed.
RWA.xyz lists Franklin’s XRP Ledger position at about $193 million, matching the share count at a dollar each. Thursday’s recorded share price puts its value nearly $8 million higher.
Brokers and custodians routinely hold shares for many clients in one account, tracking individual ownership separately.
Franklin’s fund documents describe a register combining blockchain entries with records held outside the network, including information “which links the wallet addresses of the entries on the distributed ledger to their real-world identities.”
Whether this particular wallet represents one investor or several remains unclear.
CoinDesk asked Franklin whether it is an omnibus account, how many investors funded the subscriptions and whether they or their custodians will receive tokens in separate addresses. The firm had not responded as of Asia morning hours on Saturday.
Franklin and DBS announced the fund’s Singapore-authorized structure in November 2025 with a $20 minimum investment. Initially available to wealth and accredited clients, retail access was expected in early 2026.
Their September 2025 agreement with Ripple outlined plans for eligible DBS Digital Exchange clients to switch between sgBENJI and RLUSD. DBS also said it would explore lending against the fund tokens.
Holding sgBENJI directly on XRPL requires Franklin’s approval. Its settings also allow the issuer to freeze balances and recover tokens.
Thursday’s transactions nearly quadrupled the number of sgBENJI shares on the XRP Ledger. The number of wallets holding any of them stayed at one.
