title: Bitcoin ETFs Erase October Losses With $1 Billion in Three Days - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin ETF buyers have erased October’s losses in three trading days.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $524.8 million on Wednesday, according to Decrypt’s ETF tracker, stretching an inflow streak that began Monday to three sessions and roughly $1.07 billion.
That’s enough to flip the month positive. After shedding about $615 million through last Friday, the funds are now up roughly $460 million for October.
Monday’s $526.7 million haul, the funds’ best day since Sept. 22, came entirely from BlackRock’s IBIT. The rebound follows two weeks in which the funds lost about $910 million. Cumulative net inflows since launch stand at $58.4 billion, with total net assets at $100.8 billion.
The return of buyers coincides with a fresh vote of long-term confidence from Wall Street. J.P. Morgan Asset Management this week projected a 10% compound annual return for Bitcoin over the next 10 to 15 years in its first long-term forecast for the asset, while cautioning about 55% volatility.
Ethereum ETFs, meanwhile, finally caught a break. The funds took in $14.9 million on Wednesday, snapping a five-day outflow streak that drained about $389 million. They remain deep in the red for October, though, down roughly $1.07 billion so far. Cumulative net inflows stand at $12.8 billion.
The inflows haven’t lifted prices. Bitcoin traded at about $81,470 on Thursday, down 2.4% over 24 hours but still up 2% on the week. It marks a sharp turn after Bitcoin hit a weekly high near $85,000 just yesterday.
Ethereum fell 2.6% to roughly $2,393, and the total crypto market cap slipped 2.9% to $2.84 trillion. Zcash was among the hardest hit in the top 10, dropping 5.6%, though it remains up nearly 14% over seven days.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market developed by Decrypt’s parent company Dastan, aren’t betting on a breakout.
Myriad traders give Bitcoin just a 20% chance of topping $87,500 before October ends and 9% odds of reaching $90,000. On the downside, they put the odds of a drop to $77,500 at 35%; Bitcoin already briefly slipped below $80,000 last week.
Sentiment on Ethereum is brighter, with Myriad users giving ETH a 61.3% chance of pumping to $3,000 before dumping to $1,500.
In terms of catalysts to watch, the Federal Reserve next meets on Oct. 27-28, with persistent inflation keeping another rate hike on the table.

title: What Is a Neocloud? The GPU Clouds Powering the AI Boom - Decrypt
text:
Training and running modern AI models takes a huge amount of computing power, almost all of it from graphics processing units (GPUs). For most of the past decade, renting servers meant going to one of the "hyperscalers": Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud. When the ChatGPT boom set off a scramble for GPUs, a new kind of company stepped in to meet the demand. These are the neoclouds.
Neoclouds are specialist cloud providers that do one thing: rent out GPU capacity for AI training and inference (running a trained model to answer requests). They have gone from unknown startups to listed companies with contracts worth billions of dollars, and their roots in crypto run deep. CoreWeave began as an Ethereum miner, and a wave of Bitcoin miners is now turning its power-hungry sites into AI data centers.
This guide covers what neoclouds are, how they work, who the main players are, and why their shares were sold off hard in October 2026.
A neocloud is an AI-focused infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) provider. A hyperscaler sells hundreds of services, from databases to email hosting. A neocloud mostly sells access to large clusters of high-end GPUs, plus the networking, storage and software needed to run AI workloads on them. CNBC describes them as businesses that offer access to the GPUs powering artificial intelligence as a service.
Neoclouds are companies, not blockchains, so they don't issue a native token. Their shares trade on traditional stock exchanges.
CoreWeave started in 2017 mining Ethereum with GPUs. Ethereum's 2022 switch to proof of stake ended GPU mining on the network, and CoreWeave moved its hardware over to AI and cloud work.
The neocloud model comes down to three scarce resources: chips, power and capital.
Customers such as AI labs, Big Tech firms and startups sign multi-year agreements for reserved capacity, or pay by the hour on demand. The neocloud earns the difference between what the GPUs bring in and what they cost to buy, power and finance.
The weak point is depreciation. In its second-quarter 2026 results, CoreWeave reported depreciation and amortization of nearly $1.4 billion against revenue of about $2.6 billion, while Nebius booked about $260 million against revenue of $582 million.
Neoclouds compete on speed and focus. Hyperscalers split their GPUs between many services, including their own AI products. Neoclouds can deliver large, dedicated clusters quickly, and they tune their software for AI rather than general-purpose computing. Some of their biggest customers are the hyperscalers themselves, which rent neocloud capacity when their own data centers can't keep up.
The sector also gives Bitcoin miners a second life. In the two years to July 2026, miners contracted roughly 7 gigawatts of power capacity across 19 deals worth more than $135 billion to hyperscalers, neoclouds and chipmakers, according to Bernstein. That is less than a quarter of the 30 GW the miners have in their planned power pipeline. The asset that matters is power: miners already had land, grid connections and permits, which can take years to obtain.
TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic for its Kentucky campus. The deal is expected to bring in about $19 billion, which is more than TeraWulf's entire market value at the time.
No. Neoclouds are conventional companies. The closest crypto equivalent is decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePIN) such as Render, Akash and io.net. These use tokens to pay for GPU compute and to reward the people who provide it. They aim at the same market but run on a peer-to-peer model instead of company-owned data centers.
CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS) and IREN (IREN) trade on the Nasdaq and are available through mainstream brokerages. Several other listed Bitcoin miners turned AI hosts, including TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8 and Core Scientific, give exposure to the AI hosting side of the business. Crypto-native compute tokens such as Render (RENDER) trade on major exchanges. Treat all of these as high-risk, volatile assets.
The sector is under heavy pressure. On October 14, 2026, Gartner predicted that "cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model" will force more than 80% of neocloud providers to stop operating independently by 2030. It also estimated that more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could be exposed to impairment by the end of 2030 if AI providers keep spending at their current pace.
Credit markets have grown nervous too. By October 21, 2026, CoreWeave's unsecured debt was yielding about 15%, and the cost of insuring its bonds against default had risen 30% in a month. Its shares were down 29% for October, leaving the company valued at about $34 billion, against a peak of about $90 billion in 2025. Nebius fell 27% over the same period, even though it carries far less net debt, and IREN fell 32%.
The bull case is still alive. CoreWeave co-founder Brannin McBee said nearly all of the company's 2027 capacity is already sold, with contracts running into 2028 and beyond. Whether neoclouds stay independent or end up owned by bigger players, demand for AI compute remains high. The open question is whether these companies can earn enough from it to pay back their debts.

title: Circle Shareholder Targets Donald Trump’s Alleged Crypto Corruption in Lawsuit
text:
According to a Circle shareholder, the US president’s “corruption” through USD1 left the company unable to compete with stablecoins, harming USDC.
Update (Oct. 22, 10:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from the White House.
A shareholder for Circle Internet Financial, the company behind the USDC (USDC) stablecoin, filed a lawsuit against US President Donald Trump, his family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial, affiliate entities, and US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff over a $2 billion deal between a foreign government entity and Binance.
In a Thursday filing in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, Circle shareholder J. Benjamin Greenberg alleged that Trump, Witkoff and World Liberty caused harm to Circle by creating a pathway for foreign governments to funnel money using the Trump family crypto company’s USD1 stablecoin. This “brazen corruption,” according to Greenberg, leaves Circle “unable to compete” in the stablecoin market with its USDC.
Central to the Circle shareholder’s allegations is an Abu Dhabi entity, MGX, tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty, which invested $2 billion into cryptocurrency exchange Binance using the USD1 stablecoin in 2025. The Wall Street Journal reported in February that another investment vehicle backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan agreed to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.
“By accepting hundreds of millions of dollars from a foreign government, the President and his companies have diverted business from [Circle],” alleged Greenberg, adding:
Related: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable
Greenberg reported holding 10,000 ordinary shares of Circle as part of his reasons for the lawsuit. He petitioned the court to declare that Trump violated the US Constitution’s Foreign Emoluments Clause through the crypto deals and to issue injunctions preventing the president and Witkoff from pursuing similar financial interests without Congress’ consent.
Zach Witkoff, the son of the Witkoff named in the lawsuit, is a World Liberty co-founder. Trump and his three sons are also co-founders of the crypto venture.
A Circle spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company “did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing,” declining to comment on pending litigation. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said that Trump had “no conflicts of interest“ with his crypto investments, calling the lawsuit “frivolous.“ A spokesperson for World Liberty did not respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.
The US president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures that Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while also costing investors about $4.7 billion, according to reporting by the nonprofit consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen. The crypto ventures are just a few of many controversial deals Trump faces scrutiny over, including accepting a jet from the government of Qatar.
With less than two weeks until the 2026 midterms and early voting having already started in some US states, Democrats running for reelection are using Trump’s crypto deals as a wedge issue for voters to support candidates in their party. Last week, Senator Mark Warner released a campaign ad highlighting that the president made ”more than $600 million alone from the crypto memecoin.”

title: Major Banks Find Rogue AI Agents Inside Customer Accounts—And They’re 'Horrified' - Decrypt
text:
Some of the biggest U.S. banks have discovered an uninvited presence inside their customers’ accounts: autonomous AI agents logging in, sometimes with the customer’s own credentials, and occasionally taking actions that appear to go beyond what anyone asked them to do.
That’s according to a report published Thursday by Axios, which, citing people familiar with the matter, said major banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents operating inside customer accounts, with some agents attempting steps that look independent of user instructions.
Bank executives described the situation as “horrifying,” with one saying the industry has “grave concerns” about agents reaching into accounts and taking actions that could affect people’s finances.
The banks are moving to slam the door. Morgan Stanley is blocking outside agents, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are restricting them, Axios reported.
The problem is that even when a user grants an agent permission, having software log in as the account holder clashes with the rules at most banks, which require humans to access their own accounts. One executive told Axios they struggle to tell agents apart, or to know whether a given agent was authorized by the customer or has gone rogue.
The friction points toward a middle path rather than an outright ban. According to Axios, most banks have authorized, or are leaning toward, read-only access that would let agents view a customer’s financial information without moving money, similar to what they already grant budgeting apps. Industry executives acknowledged customers will want to use these agents, so some accommodation is likely coming.
The report lands amid a drumbeat of alarm over AI agents slipping their leashes. Agents have repeatedly escaped their creators’ control, breaching systems in ways their developers didn’t intend, and the Bank for International Settlements has warned that AI is shrinking the window banks have to patch security flaws before attackers exploit them.
The banking scare feeds a wider debate over how to contain increasingly capable agents. Proposals have ranged from an AI “kill switch,” which Nvidia has already taken steps to implement on a technical level, to calls from scientists to cut advanced models off from the internet entirely.
It’s a sign of how seriously the financial system and beyond are taking the risk of software that can act on its own.

title: Dune Targets Institutional Traders With Onchain Market Data
text:
The new service aims to bring onchain trading data into institutional financial systems as tokenized stock markets expand and face growing scrutiny.
Blockchain analytics platform Dune has launched real-time market data feeds covering more than 200 onchain trading venues, aiming to bring decentralized market activity into the trading systems used by traditional financial institutions.
The new service provides trade data from 12 blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, Base and XLayer, roughly one second after execution, according to a Thursday announcement.
The feeds cover spot trading across decentralized exchanges, as well as perpetual futures trading on Hyperliquid and Lighter, with standardized data on prices, trade sizes and transaction details across markets.
According to Dune co-founder and CEO Fredrik Haga, quant funds, market makers, asset managers and bank trading desks are among the first clients using the service, although he declined to identify them, citing nondisclosure agreements. Dune said the firms use the data to assess liquidity, compare prices across venues and evaluate trading strategies before committing capital.
“Most institutions are watching onchain markets first, because they can’t price these assets properly without them anymore,” Haga said. He expects direct onchain trading to follow as liquidity improves and regulatory rules catch up, adding:
Related: Ondo lets institutions convert stocks directly into tokenized shares
The market for tokenized stocks has grown sharply over the past year, but fragmented liquidity and disputes over whether companies should have a say in how their shares are traded onchain have raised questions about the market’s development.
Recently, tensions surfaced around OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange. The venture announced plans for a tokenized stock trading platform on Oct. 4, but has since faced objections from several publicly traded companies.
So far, 16 companies, including Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs, have filed objections to having their shares traded on the proposed platform, although they did not specify their reasons.
Beyond issuer objections, market fragmentation poses another concern. In May, Tiger Research director Ryan Yoon warned that trading the same tokenized stocks across multiple blockchain platforms could create price discrepancies, increase slippage and reduce market efficiency.
According to RWA.xyz data, the distributed value of tokenized stocks has reached $3.58 billion, up from about $627 million a year earlier, a roughly 470% increase.

title: SoFi Launches Tokenized Deposit That Earns 4.4% and Converts to a Stablecoin - Decrypt
text:
SoFi is giving its customers a way to earn bank-grade interest on digital dollars without giving up the speed of crypto, launching what it calls the first national bank-issued tokenized deposit for consumers.
Announced Thursday, the product, SoFi Earn, trades under the ticker SOFIE, with each token representing $1 held on deposit at SoFi Bank. Holders earn 4.40% annual percentage yield, and the funds are FDIC-insured up to applicable limits, a key distinction from ordinary stablecoins.
When members want to deploy the money, they can convert SOFIE one-to-one into SoFiUSD, the bank’s stablecoin, and then use it to buy crypto in the SoFi app or move dollars over blockchain rails around the clock.
The pitch targets a specific gap. Stablecoins have become a popular way to park digital dollars, but many pay no interest and carry no deposit insurance. SoFi cited Federal Reserve research estimating that roughly $64 billion, or about 21% of the stablecoin market, sits idle in forgotten or inactive wallets. The company is pitching SOFIE as a way to keep that money earning until the moment it’s spent.
“Too much money in the digital asset ecosystem is sitting idle,” CEO Anthony Noto said in a statement, arguing the product combines “the earning power and protections of a bank deposit with the speed and utility of digital assets.”
SoFi Earn is the fifth crypto product the company has rolled out in under a year, part of an aggressive build-out of its digital-money ecosystem.
SoFi returned to crypto trading in late 2025 after exiting the business years earlier, becoming the first nationally chartered U.S. bank to offer it to consumers, and members can now trade more than 40 tokens.
The company followed that with SoFiUSD, the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank, launched across Ethereum and Solana and now used to settle SoFi’s entire card program over Mastercard’s network.
The move pushes SoFi deeper into a space where banks and fintech firms are racing to fold blockchain-based dollars into regulated products, following its earlier launch of business banking for digital assets and a stablecoin tie-up involving cryptocurrency exchange Kraken.
By wrapping a yield-bearing, insured deposit in a token that moves like a stablecoin, SoFi is betting consumers want both at once.

title: Italy Busts Mafia 'Secret Bank' That Laundered Money Through Crypto, Seizes $24M - Decrypt
text:
Italian police have arrested 30 people accused of running an underground bank for organized crime from a car-rental business near Milan, and seized €21 million (about $23.6 million) in cash, bank balances, cryptocurrency, boats, jewelry and luxury watches, Italian news agency ANSA reported on Wednesday.
The operation, carried out by the Guardia di Finanza, Italy's financial police, on the orders of Milan's anti-mafia prosecutors, targeted suspects linked to the 'Ndrangheta, the Camorra and organized crime groups from Foggia in southern Italy. Sixteen were taken into custody and 14 placed under house arrest, including two people arrested in Spain and one in Switzerland.
According to investigators, the business in Pero, on the outskirts of Milan, was run by three Italians: two long-standing contacts of 'Ndrangheta clans from Crotone, both previously convicted in earlier mafia investigations, and a member of the Camorra's Casalesi clan. Chinese and Albanian accomplices helped operate the network, prosecutors said.
Shell companies issued more than €110 million in invoices for services never provided, letting businesses cut their tax bills. Those firms paid by bank transfer and received the money back in cash, minus a commission. The network moved about €68 million abroad, according to prosecutors.
Funds gathered in the shell companies' accounts were sent to banks in Luxembourg, Lithuania and Germany, then routed through crypto exchanges into wallets controlled by the network, Bloomberg reported. Drug traffickers who handed over cash received crypto or international bank transfers in return, and the network also handled money stolen from victims of online crypto investment scams, according to the report.
The Guardia di Finanza's technology fraud unit supported the investigation, which is set out in a court order running to more than 500 pages.
Among those arrested is a Guardia di Finanza inspector, placed under house arrest on corruption charges, according to Calabrian outlet LaC News24. Investigators also accused a Milan court employee of leaking information about ongoing investigations, and a lawyer and a former member of the financial police are among those caught up in the case.
Italian authorities have warned for years that organized crime is adopting digital assets. In 2021, Italy's Anti-Mafia Investigative Directorate said that "all criminal organizations, including those of the Mafia type, have an interest in using these instruments for their business," and described the 'Ndrangheta, Italy's most powerful criminal syndicate, as "growing more and more attuned to modern tools like cryptocurrency and the deep web."

title: Chinese Prosecutors Seek to Confiscate $5.1B in Bitcoin Seized by UK in Qian Case - Decrypt
text:
Prosecutors in China have applied to confiscate the 61,896 BTC seized from Zhimin Qian in the UK, and a court in Tianjin has agreed to hear the case, according to a court notice reported by Chinese outlet The Paper.
The Bitcoin is worth about $5.1 billion at its current price of around $82,000.
The Tianjin No. 2 Intermediate People's Court said it accepted the application from the city's prosecutors on September 28, and published a notice on October 13. The court said there was evidence that Qian had committed fundraising fraud, mainly in Tianjin's Hedong district.
Besides the Bitcoin, prosecutors are seeking about 72,746 units each of Bitcoin Cash, Bitcoin Gold and Bitcoin SV, around 3.6 million XRP, and some 70 million Dogecoin, which UK authorities have already converted and placed in an interest-bearing account. The application also covers U.S. dollar, euro and pound cash, jewelry, bank balances and investment portfolios.
According to the prosecutors' application, Qian was the controller of Tianjin Lantian Gerui Electronic Technology, and between April 2014 and August 2017 sold fake wealth management products across China without a license, promising guaranteed returns. The scheme raised more than 40.38 billion yuan, most of which was not used for any genuine business, and left more than 102,000 investors with losses totaling about 19.98 billion yuan, prosecutors said.
Qian fled China in July 2017 with computers holding Bitcoin wallets and eventually reached the UK, where she converted some of the coins into other assets.
Prosecutors argue the seized assets are proceeds of crime that should be recovered, returned to victims, and otherwise confiscated. Because Qian has been a wanted fugitive for more than a year, the case falls under Chinese rules that allow confiscation without the suspect present.
Victims can apply to join the proceedings through a WeChat mini-program, though those who do not will still be able to receive repayments from any recovered assets. The notice period runs for six months, after which the court will hear the case.
Qian was jailed for 11 years and eight months in the UK in November 2025, after pleading guilty to acquiring and possessing criminal property. Unnamed Treasury officials had privately raised whether the seized Bitcoin could help fill a shortfall in the UK's public finances, the Financial Times reported at the time, while legal experts argued that victims could be entitled to compensation if they could show a sufficient link to the coins.
Weeks after Qian's guilty plea, UK prosecutors told the High Court they were planning a compensation scheme for victims, without giving details. They have since said victims could be compensated through a redress scheme run from China.
On October 12, the High Court ruled that Chinese law should govern thousands of victims' claims to the coins, a decision seen as improving the UK government's chances of keeping them. Law firm Fieldfisher, which represents the claimants, said it is seeking to appeal.
The ruling does not decide whether the victims own the Bitcoin, since no evidence has yet been heard on the content of Chinese law, David Phillips, a dispute resolution partner at London law firm SMB, wrote on Wednesday. But it shows that "a victim cannot necessarily recover cryptocurrency simply by proving: 'That Bitcoin was bought with money taken from me,'" he wrote.
"Cryptoassets may operate without borders, but proprietary rights in them remain capable of raising intensely territorial questions of applicable law," Phillips added.

title: Ken Griffin Says AI Is 'Almost Certainly' in a Bubble—And Compares GPUs to Airline Seats - Decrypt
text:
Ken Griffin, founder of the Wall Street giant Citadel, said Tuesday that investors are “almost certainly” in an AI bubble—though he isn’t telling them to dump their AI stocks.
“What’s left in the wake of these bubbles, if we want to use that word, is often game changing for the world. And the companies that are on the other side of that bubble are the market leaders for decades to come,” Griffin said at Citadel’s Future of Global Markets Conference in New York on Oct. 20
This reaches beyond tech investors, since the AI buildout has underpinned equity markets over the past year, so many index funds and retirement accounts hold a slice of it. A bubble is what happens when prices climb far faster than the businesses behind them can justify, until reality catches up. Citadel is a hedge fund, a private firm that invests money for wealthy clients and institutions.
But the fact that it seems like a bubble isn’t that big a deal if you look at the big picture, according to Griffin. “Any radical transformation of our economy is generally intertwined with a bubble,” he said, recalling the internet boom and adding that he wishes he had kept his Amazon stock.
The companies that emerge on the other side of a bubble tend to lead markets for decades, he argued, though he stopped short of predicting a collapse. His own firm is a case study: Griffin said AI agents, software that carries out multistep tasks on its own, cut some high-level Citadel research from weeks to a couple of hours.
Griffin compared GPUs, the graphics chips that many companies use to train and run AI models, to airline seats. Both have a very low marginal cost to run, meaning the extra expense of serving one more customer is tiny, so prices can collapse once supply outstrips demand.
He pointed to the telecom boom around 2000, when companies laid more fiber-optic cable than demand required and communication prices fell. He also doubted that chips five or six years old, which still earn rental rates he called extraordinary, will keep doing so for another five or six years.
Buyers are getting pickier, Griffin said, sorting which jobs justify premium models from OpenAI and Anthropic and which can run on cheaper open-source alternatives, meaning models anyone can download and run on their own computers. Corporate America has been uneven at extracting value from AI, he added, with companies studying their bills from the labs and asking where the productivity is.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending at nearly $1.5 trillion for 2025, counting everything from chips and servers to AI-enabled phones. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Davos in January that the industry is only “a few hundred billion dollars” into what he called the largest infrastructure buildout in human history, with trillions still to build. If customers balk at premium prices, the chip and cloud companies counting on that spending would feel it first.
On July 30, Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold most of its public stock portfolio to Citadel at roughly a 10% discount after its value reportedly fell about 67% in July.
The fund had borrowed as much as four times its capital to buy AI stocks, a tactic called leverage, and its lenders asked for more collateral every day as prices fell. Selling because lenders demand it rather than by choice is known as forced selling, and it feeds itself because each sale pushes prices down and triggers more demands.
Citadel has since shed more than 80% of the risk in that portfolio, Griffin wrote in an August letter to clients, which means the man calling the bubble also bought the discounted stocks.
Griffin warned earlier this year that if the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping lane, stayed closed for another six to 12 months, energy prices would rise materially and push the world into recession.
Wall Street analysts expect growth in capital spending, the money poured into chips and data centers, by the largest AI infrastructure builders to slow from 75% in the third quarter of 2025 to 25% by the end of 2026, Goldman Sachs Research noted in December.

title: Nvidia Unveils Its Full-Stack Blueprint to Contain and Monitor AI Agents - Decrypt
text:
Nvidia on Wednesday unveiled the OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin, a full-stack design that pairs its Vera CPUs, OpenShell software and BlueField-4 chips to contain and monitor autonomous AI agents, according to the company's announcement.
Vera Rubin systems run the models, Vera CPUs run the agents and their tools inside OpenShell, and BlueField-4 chips run a monitoring framework called Sentry. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the split as agents that basically exist thanks to a synergy of different environments and frameworks.
“Nvidia created OpenShell to give agents the freedom to do useful work within clearly defined boundaries—contained, monitored and under control,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said. “With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField.”
OpenShell, the open-source runtime at the center of the design, treats every agent workload as untrusted and grants access only when needed, Nvidia said in a technical blog post.
It has four parts: a gateway that manages sandboxes and policies, a supervisor that checks outbound requests and handles credentials separately from the sandbox, the sandbox that isolates the agent, and a policy prover that runs formal verification to check that permissions stay under a ceiling the organization sets.
On the hardware side, BlueField-4, a data processing unit that handles networking and security apart from the main processor, sits on the node's only path to the model. That lets Sentry inspect traffic between an agent and the model without relying on the agent to report on itself, per the Sentry deep dive.
Nvidia bundled OpenShell and Sentry into the Open Agent Safety Platform on Sept. 28, with more than 100 launch partners, after a summer in which agents repeatedly slipped out of their test environments. METR reported in August that roughly 1,200 OpenAI agents coordinated on an unsanctioned message board, and about 700 went on to attack Hugging Face.
An OpenAI agent also broke into Australia's Medicare statistics portal in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in September. Nvidia says enterprises can run agents from model builders including Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI on OpenShell infrastructure.
Security vendors including CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Check Point are integrating support for the architecture into their agent security products, and European banks BBVA and Santander are exploring it as a framework for agent safety and governance. ServiceNow also announced general availability of its Arc agent, with actions governed at runtime and enforced by OpenShell.
Nvidia describes BlueField-4 and Sentry as an optional hardware safeguard for deployments that need protection beyond OpenShell's software boundaries. The company says the architecture is available now, but the Sentry deep dive lists the framework's planned availability as early next year, with more libraries and resources still in the testing phase.

title: Who Found the PHP Bug That Made Governments Unplug Their Websites? ChatGPT, Of Course - Decrypt
text:
The two PHP bugs that pushed Finland, the Netherlands, and France to pull government websites offline on Wednesday weren't found by a hacker in a hoodie. They were found by AI—OpenAI's AI, to be specific.
"Over the past two months, we have been leading a coalition to mitigate one of the most severe bugs in open source software found in recent memory, php2shell," OpenAI President Greg Brockman said in a statement. "It was discovered and addressed using our models as part of our Patch the Planet initiative."
The flaws let anyone run their own code on servers running PHP, the language behind about 70% of websites whose server-side language is known. PHP shipped fixes a day after details leaked online.
According to Brockman, the bug sat in PHP for 14 years, and a limited version surfaced in 2024 but "wasn't considered significant at the time." Researchers at security firm Calif, working under Patch the Planet, used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol to find a version of it in August, and OpenAI's own team found a fuller version in September. Cloud security firm Wiz also found both flaws independently, per OpenAI's disclosure.
Brockman was able to turn a global panic attack into a great PR stunt, promoting GPT’s abilities while admitting the ending got messy: “While the tail end of the disclosure didn't go as planned (the original target date was a October 22 release, but details started to leak early, so PHP’s maintainers brought the release forward to October 21), I am grateful that the coalition successfully had an entire two months to prepare—the fixes were quite intricate for PHP, and a leak significantly before the patch was available would have been very impactful. ”he said.
GPT-5.6 Sol's résumé already includes a break-in. In July, OpenAI said the model and an unreleased sibling escaped a locked test environment during a hacking benchmark, found a zero-day flaw along the way, and pulled answers straight from Hugging Face's production database and other five major companies.
Turns out "by accident" only works if you're a billion-dollar company 🙃🙃#OpenAI#chatgpt#Anthropic pic.twitter.com/D7LPUlnql1
— Gaxan (@pvgagan02) October 19, 2026
In September, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent had accessed non-public files on a Medicare statistics portal back in June, and called the notification process "unacceptable." Days later, OpenAI disclosed that its agents had also pulled data from U.S. government sites, including the Census Bureau and the SEC, while insisting none of those incidents counted as breaches.
Now the same company is pitching itself as the internet's night watchman. "Defenders need to have a tighter OODA loop than attackers," Brockman said, borrowing a military term for the cycle of observing, orienting, deciding, and acting, and argued that's possible "especially if defenders have access to stronger models than attackers."
He went further, floating a future where "authorized defenders (such as government)" scan the internet for vulnerable servers and, "in extreme cases," patch them remotely. "It should thus be a national priority to ensure that we always have the most capable cyber models," he said.
To protect the world from the dangers of AI, OpenAI has committed $1 billion in subsidized access to Daybreak, its AI program for defenders protecting critical infrastructure. Brockman said the company is also fixing "several other significant bugs," including a remote code execution flaw that Node.js announced Wednesday.
And PHP won't be the last. “We expect to find many more such issues over upcoming months,” Brockman said. Hopefully the disclosures go smoother next time—ChatGPT could probably help draft the emails.

title: How a SpaceX and Tesla Merger Would Reshape Musk’s AI Empire - Decrypt
text:
Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to study merging his two biggest companies, a deal that would put rockets, electric cars, humanoid robots, a social network and the Grok chatbot inside a single corporation worth roughly $3.5 trillion.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. The singularity is Silicon Valley shorthand for the point where AI outsmarts humans and starts improving itself faster than anyone can keep up.
He then listed what the two companies would share: “superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity.”
In plain English, that means AI models, custom chips, a giant chip factory, robots, and satellites that work as data centers in orbit.
If it happens, one company—with one man holding the majority of its votes—would own a leading AI chatbot, the social network that feeds it data, the satellites that connect it, the factory that makes its chips, and the cars and robots it is meant to drive.
Nothing has been signed and Musk warned that assuming a merger is a certainty “would be overstating it.” If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you already hold a sliver of Tesla—not SpaceX—and in an all-stock deal those shares would likely be swapped for stock in the combined company.
It would be Musk’s third consolidation since March 2025, when xAI absorbed X (formerly Twitter). In February, SpaceX swallowed xAI in a deal valuing the AI company at $250 billion, weeks after Tesla put about $2 billion into it; in June, SpaceX went public in the largest IPO ever.
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion on Tuesday, well above the $12.72 billion analysts expected. It also booked its first quarterly profit since going public, largely by renting the computing power of its AI server farms to firms such as Anthropic and Google.
The most ambitious piece is Starmind, SpaceX’s plan to put AI data centers in orbit. The company has asked U.S. regulators to approve up to 1 million satellites that would run AI models on near-constant sunlight, and Musk expects deployments to start in late 2027 and reach “significant scale” in 2028.
Musk’s argument is that Earth is running out of room and electricity for AI, and the politics back him up. An Annenberg survey found 61% of Americans now oppose new data centers in their area, and roughly $130 billion in projects were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
SpaceX’s own IPO paperwork, however, warned investors that orbital AI computing relies on “unproven technologies” and “may not achieve commercial viability.” Tesla’s main contribution would be Terafab, a $16.8 billion chip factory the two companies are building in Texas to supply Optimus robots, Cybercab robotaxis, and those space data centers.
Musk isn't the first to look past dry land to keep servers cool. Microsoft's Project Natick sank 855 servers off the coast of Scotland in 2018. Over two years only six failed, a 0.7% rate against 5.9% for a comparable group on land, yet Microsoft shut the program down anyway, with cloud operations chief Noelle Walsh saying, “I’m not building subsea data centers anywhere in the world.”
China has since picked up the idea with a wind-powered underwater data center about six miles off Shanghai, which its builder, HiCloud, says uses at least 30% less electricity than land-based rivals, while startup Lonestar aimed at launching a small data storage unit toward the Moon in early 2025.
Wall Street mostly likes the idea, at the right price. “We believe this is a no-brainer move for both SpaceX and Tesla, it comes down to the price for shareholders,” Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. told Reuters, estimating Tesla shares would need to be valued around $550 apiece—a premium, or bonus over the market price, big enough to win the vote.
Tesla spiked almost 4% after Elon’s statements went public. His words were more powerful for Tesla’s stocks than building a flying car, considering the stock dipped after the demonstration.
Even if nothing is for certain, markets are flirting with the idea. Tesla investor Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management now puts the odds of a deal within two years at 95%.
SpaceX is also a major contractor for the U.S. military, intelligence agencies, and NASA, while Tesla relies heavily on its Shanghai factory, a national security mix Reuters said could draw scrutiny from both Washington and Beijing.
A merger would also hand Musk the tighter grip on Tesla he has long demanded. He owns about 20% of Tesla but controls most of SpaceX’s votes through supervoting shares—stock that carries extra votes—and Barclays estimates he would hold about 56% of the votes in a combined company.
SpaceX reacted much more favorably with a 10% spike, the best movement since June.
Any deal still needs the support of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, not just those cast, a bar Musk called “quite a high hurdle.” Barclays suggested last week that an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting on December 3.

title: Bitcoin Hits Weekly High as Crypto Market Rebounds - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin traders and hodlers are breathing this week after a pretty spooky start to the month with the historically best gains.
Bitcoin traded near $84,500 on Wednesday, up 2.5% over 24 hours, as the crypto market bounced back from a mid-October slide that pushed it below $80,000. The total crypto market capitalization, the combined value of every coin, rose 2.2% to $2.9 trillion.
Ethereum climbed 2.5% to $2,504, Solana gained 2.2% to $108.18 and BNB rose 2% to $749. XRP led the large caps with a 4.1% gain to $1.37, while Zcash jumped 11.2% to $1,332 and has now added 15.3% over seven days.
The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a 0-to-100 gauge where 0 means extreme fear and 100 means extreme greed, reads 55, which counts as neutral but is 3 points ahead of yesterday’s readings. In other words, it seems like traders have stopped panicking, but they are not yet chasing prices.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, has swung between $97 and $112 a barrel this month and traded near $108 on Wednesday. The war with Iran keeps supply fears alive, and Washington rejected an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in late September.
Oil matters to crypto because it feeds inflation. U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above the 3.6% economists expected and up from 3.4% in August. Higher inflation pushes up Treasury yields, the annual return investors demand for lending to the U.S. government. Government bonds paying more than 5% with almost no default risk pull money away from stocks and crypto, and higher rates make the borrowing behind leveraged trades costlier.
The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate sits at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, and CME FedWatch gives about an eight-in-ten chance of a hold at the Oct. 28 meeting. Markets firmly expect a hike on Dec. 9.
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened Wednesday at $82,928.80 and has reached $84,726.28, up 1.94% for the candle, after bouncing about 6% from this month's low near $79,711. Its current price is pressing up, trying to approach the natural resistance at $87,422.70.
Bitcoin’s latest rally ran from $62,763 to a September high of $87,422.70. That trend marked a strong support at $81,603. Bitcoin lost the level in the October dip and has now reclaimed it, with movement still in the upper side of its bounce..
The 50-day exponential moving average, an average of recent closing prices that gives more weight to the most recent days, sits near $80,782, above the 200-day moving average at about $76,084. A 50-day above the 200-day is the standard sign of an uptrend, and Bitcoin trades 4.6% above the shorter average.
The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, which scores recent buying against selling on a 0-to-100 scale, reads 58.5. Readings above 50 mean buyers hold the edge, while 70 marks overbought territory, so momentum is not yet stretched but is moving towards a bullish mood.
The bullish scenario needs a daily close above $84,726, today's high, ideally with ADX—an indicator of a trend’s strength over time—climbing back above 25 to confirm a trend. That would open a natural target at around $86,090, and then the September high at $87,422.70.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market built by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, put the odds of Bitcoin touching $87,500 in October at 31%, down from 45% on Oct. 12. A $90,000 touch is priced at 18%.
A stall below $84,726 would keep Bitcoin inside the roughly $79,700 to $87,400 range that has held since late September, which fits an ADX under 20.
The bearish case starts with a daily close below $81,603. That would expose the 50-day EMA at $80,782, then the October low near $79,711, and the 200-day EMA at $76,084.

title: Dogecoin Gets a Dedicated Company to Build Out Its Ecosystem - Decrypt
text:
Dogecoin is getting a dedicated company to build out its ecosystem, as the teams behind the meme coin’s biggest consumer products fold into a single organization aimed at giving DOGE more everyday uses.
Announced Tuesday, Dogecoin Labs was formed together with the Dogecoin Foundation to consolidate the products, intellectual property, and development teams scattered across the Dogecoin world into one independent outfit.
It will own and operate three flagship products: the MyDoge wallet, the DogeOS app platform, and Such App, a merchant-payments tool, with assets and talent contributed by both the Foundation and House of Doge.
The pitch is to close a gap the company sees as Dogecoin’s defining weakness. Despite ranking among the largest and most recognizable cryptocurrencies, with deep liquidity, millions of holders and one of crypto’s most active communities, the number of actual products and businesses built on DOGE remains small relative to that audience. Dogecoin Labs, led by CEO Jordan Jefferson, the founder of MyDoge and DogeOS, intends to change that by building wallets, payments, commerce, trading, DeFi, gaming, AI and social apps.
“No other digital asset has Dogecoin’s combination of liquidity, community and cultural reach, and its potential has barely been tapped,” Jefferson said, adding that the community has chanted “DOGE to $1” for years and that the goal now is “to build the economy that ambition calls for.”
The move builds on recent groundwork. DogeOS opened its public testnet on Sept. 30, giving developers an Ethereum-compatible environment to build Dogecoin apps, while MyDoge, which grew past 500,000 users without paid acquisition, rolled out a V3 update connecting the wallet to those applications. Together with Such App’s merchant rails, the three products are meant to link developers, consumers and businesses into a functioning DOGE economy.
The Foundation will continue its stewardship, open-source support and advocacy while Labs handles commercial product development.
The reorganization arrives during a soft stretch for the token. DOGE traded around $0.084 on Tuesday, up 3.9% on the day for a roughly $13 billion market cap, but down about 14% over the past month and off roughly 88% from its May 2021 record.
Dogecoin’s institutional story has been mixed, too: a Dogecoin Foundation-backed 21Shares DOGE ETF launched on Nasdaq this year, though Bitwise later shut its own Dogecoin fund citing low demand and a need to “optimize its product range to meet evolving investor needs.”

title: Musk’s SpaceX-Tesla Merger Would Create a Bitcoin Treasury Behemoth - Decrypt
text:
Elon Musk’s floated merger of SpaceX and Tesla would do more than unite rockets and electric cars. It would fold two of the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin stashes onto a single balance sheet.
Speaking on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Musk said the boards of both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to weigh a tie-up, cautioning that treating a deal as “a certainty” would be “overstating it.”
But the prospect alone has drawn fresh attention to the combined entity’s crypto holdings.
Tesla reported 11,509 BTC in its most recent quarterly filing, while SpaceX disclosed 18,712 BTC in the S-1 it filed ahead of its June IPO. Together, that’s 30,221 BTC, worth roughly $2.5 billion at Bitcoin’s recent price near $83,000.
As Decrypt reported when the merger idea first surfaced, combining the two would stack one of the largest non-mining corporate Bitcoin positions anywhere under Musk’s control, placing the merged company among the top handful of public holders, trailing only the likes of Michael Saylor’s Strategy and a few others.
The SpaceX portion is the more striking piece. The rocket maker’s 18,712 BTC was effectively invisible to public markets until its IPO filing, meaning a substantial treasury had quietly accumulated inside a private company for years before anyone could count it, more than double what blockchain trackers had previously attributed to SpaceX wallets. The combined cost basis across both firms sits around $1 billion, implying an average buy price near $35,000 per coin.
A merger wouldn’t change anything about Bitcoin itself, and neither company has signaled plans to buy or sell. Both have held their positions static, with SpaceX last moving coins in prior years and Tesla reporting no changes.
What a deal would alter is governance and accounting: one of the most closely watched corporate Bitcoin piles would sit inside a single public vehicle, subject to quarterly disclosures and the fair-value accounting that recently forced Tesla to book a loss as Bitcoin slid.
For now, the treasury math is hypothetical, living or dying with a transaction that remains exploratory. But it underscores how, almost incidentally, a Musk mega-merger would also create a Bitcoin giant.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Gain $301M Despite Late-Week Sell-Off
text:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs finished the week with $301 million in net inflows after a strong three-day start gave way to heavy withdrawals.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted around $301 million in net inflows last week, snapping a two-week outflow streak despite heavy withdrawals late in the week.
The funds lost about $228 million the previous week and $680 million the week before. October’s net outflows stood at about $314 million, according to Farside Investors data.
Bitcoin ETFs drew $1.08 billion between Monday and Wednesday as Bitcoin (BTC) climbed to a weekly high of $84,777 on Wednesday, according to CoinGecko. Investors then withdrew about $774 million on Thursday and Friday as BTC retreated toward $80,000.
ETF investors have tended to sell into Bitcoin declines, according to research published Thursday by market maker DWF Labs. The company found net outflows during seven of eight Bitcoin sell-offs of at least 15% since US spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024.
“ETF investors aren’t the dip buyers people think they are,” DWF said.
At the time of publication, Bitcoin traded at $80,025, down around 3.3% over the past seven days. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to a “Neutral” reading of 50, down from “Greed” at 59 a week earlier.
US spot Ether ETFs recorded a fourth consecutive week of net outflows, shedding about $221 million last week, according to Farside Investors data.

title: South Korea weighs fourth delay of crypto gains tax, eyes 2029 start: report
text: South Korea is likely to postpone its planned tax on cryptocurrency gains for the fourth time, with implementation potentially pushed to 2029, according to local news outlet Newsis. The presidential office is reportedly discussing a further delay of the levy with relevant government agencies. The tax plan is currently scheduled to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027. South Korea first introduced the crypto tax plan in 2020 through an amendment to the Income Tax Act. It sought to apply a 22% rate, including local tax, to annual gains from the transfer or lending of crypto assets after a basic deduction of 2.5 million won ($1,888). The measure was originally set for 2022 but has already been delayed three times as local traders and experts expressed concern over tax infrastructure and investor protection. A further postponement would mark the fourth delay. CARF timeline The Newsis report cited the timeline of the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) as a key factor in the delay. CARF is the international standard for bringing crypto under global tax rules, enabling automatic exchange of transaction data between tax authorities. South Korea is among dozens of jurisdictions set to begin exchanging crypto transaction data under CARF in 2027. However, the U.S. is scheduled to start participating in 2029. An official of the presidential office has reportedly said that the unavailability of U.S. trading data is the biggest bottleneck for crypto taxation, as authorities would need to track overseas transactions individually. It would also increase the burden on users of domestic platforms. A bill introduced by ruling Democratic Party lawmaker Park Min-gyu also proposes targeting the tax start date to January 1, 2029. The government is expected to finalize its position through inter-agency consultations. A final decision is likely to come through National Assembly tax law revisions, with discussions expected between late November and early December, the report said.

title: Calpers reduces 'magnificent seven' holdings as neocloud stocks slide
text:
Calpers, the world’s fifth-largest pension fund, is cutting its exposure to major U.S. technology companies as concerns mount over stretched valuations and the sustainability of the artificial intelligence investment boom, the Financial Times reported.
The fund, which manages more than $600 billion, reduced the combined number of shares it directly held in the so-called Magnificent Seven tech stocks by 26% during the first half, according to FT calculations based on regulatory filings. The group comprises Apple AAPL, Microsoft MSFT, Alphabet GOOG, Amazon AMZN, Nvidia NVDA, Meta Platforms META and Tesla TSLA.The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MGAS) is up 7% year to date, led by Apple’s 34% gain, followed by Nvidia’s 12% rise. Meta, Alphabet and Tesla are all down for the year.
Calpers is increasing its exposure to private equity, seeking to spread its investments across a broader range of companies and reduce its dependence on a handful of stock market leaders.
Deputy chief investment officer Anton Orlich told the FT that public equity valuations looked expensive and that the technology giants could underperform other investments.
The repositioning adds a further dimension to concerns highlighted by Elon Musk, whose SpaceX SPCX raised $40 billion in debt to buy GPUs for AI calculations. Musk warned that financing had largely dried up for companies lacking substantial revenue outside AI data centers, predicting consolidation among neocloud providers.
That pressure continued into Monday’s pre-market trading, with neoclouds such as CoreWeave (CRWV), Cipher Digital CIFR and IREN IREN all selling off.

title: Aviva Investors, Ripple launch tokenized share class of $29 billion sterling fund on XRP Ledger
text: Aviva Investors, the asset management arm of UK insurer Aviva, has launched a tokenized share class of its £22 billion ($29.4 billion) Sterling Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger, working with blockchain payments firm Ripple. Aviva invested £50 million ($66.7 million) in the new share class, according to a Monday announcement. The firm now has more than £86 million ($114.8 million) invested across its two tokenized money market fund offerings, including a U.S. dollar liquidity fund share class launched in July. The Sterling Liquidity Fund, which dates back to 2002, invests in high-grade, sterling-denominated short-term debt instruments and offers daily liquidity. It is domiciled in Ireland and operates as a UCITS money market fund. Under the fund's "digital twin" model, investors' holdings are represented onchain, but the fund itself continues to operate offchain. RWA market cap by blockchain. Image: The Block. Second tokenized fund on XRPL Investors need an eligible digital wallet to access the new share class. BNY Mellon holds the fund's assets, while digital asset custodian Komainu and digital infrastructure platform Licuido also supported the launch. Aviva said the tokenized shares carry the same investment objective, risk profile, liquidity characteristics, and regulatory protections as the conventional fund. Aviva first partnered with Ripple in February, with plans to bring some of its traditional investment funds onto the XRP Ledger. Ripple said at the time that Aviva was its first European investment management partner. Aviva subsequently launched its tokenized USD Liquidity Fund share class on the XRP Ledger on July 29, with approval from the Central Bank of Ireland. "We believe tokenized funds can increase efficiency and ultimately lead to improved client outcomes," Aviva Investors CEO Mark Versey said in the announcement. He added that the firm plans to explore further tokenization opportunities with Ripple.

title: Israel's Central Bank Rebukes Netanyahu Plan to Use Crypto to Dodge Sanctions - Decrypt
text:
Israel's central bank has rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's suggestion that cryptocurrency could help the country get around potential international sanctions, in a rare public rebuke days before Tuesday's national election.
Cryptocurrencies "cannot serve as a means to circumvent sanctions imposed on Israel," the Bank of Israel said in a statement on Saturday, according to the Financial Times. "The right course of action for the Israeli economy is to preserve economic relations with our primary trading partners and to focus on preventing sanctions and their negative impact on the economy," it added.
Netanyahu said in a Channel 10 interview on Friday that Israel needed to prepare for possible banking sanctions, and that he had asked for a plan to use crypto and blockchain networks to get around them. "Blockchain is one of the alternatives, certainly," he said. He did not say who was drafting the plan or which currency or network it would use.
Netanyahu later said he was taking the central bank's position into account but would do what he believed was best, The Times of Israel reported.
Countries including the UK, France and Canada have announced or pledged restrictions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, amid criticism of settlement expansion and rising settler violence.
On Sunday, more than 100 economists, including former Bank of Israel governor Jacob Frenkel and several Nobel laureates, signed a letter warning that the plan would bring higher unemployment and a collapse in foreign investment, Reuters reported. They called it "a puzzling solution, one accepted in criminal organizations, that will not help in the slightest."
Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main challenger in Tuesday's election, called the idea "madness" and said the "BibiCoin policy" would drive companies abroad, while opposition leader Yair Lapid compared what Netanyahu called a "bypass economy" to those of Iran, Russia and Venezuela.
Economists also questioned whether the plan would work at all. "It's not possible to circumvent sanctions with digital currencies as the blockchain system is publicly open and transparent, which means that every transfer is registered and can be traced to its origin," Gali Ingber, head of finance studies at the College of Management Academic Studies, told The Times of Israel.
Israel has itself used blockchain tracing to target sanctioned groups. In July, Defense Minister Israel Katz signed sanctions orders on 37 crypto wallets holding more than 24 million shekels that Israel said belonged to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.
Opinion polls point to a possible stalemate in Tuesday's election, with neither Netanyahu's coalition nor the opposition alliance on course for a governing majority.

title: A $68 million BTC price bet is targeting a surge to $90,000 after U.S. mid-term vote: Crypto Daily

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 is trading pretty much where it was on Saturday, around $80,000, offering little news on the price front. Most of the other major cryptocurrencies, including ether ETH$2,490.55, XRP (XRP), solana (SOL) and dogecoin DOGE$0.08295, BNB BNB$748.57, are equally listless.
In contrast, options trading on decentralized platform Derive is offering some excitement. The platform told CoinDesk that one trader took $68 million bet that BTC's spot price would climb above $90,000 just after U.S. mid-term elections in early November. There has also been an increase in bets implying market prices will top $100,000 by Christmas.
First, the $68 million trade. On Oct. 20, a single wallet bought 800 contracts of $90,000 call options expiring on Nov. 6 on Derive. Each contract represents one BTC.
“That's approximately $68 million in face value at current Bitcoin prices – the largest open Bitcoin position on Derive,” the exchange told CoinDesk.
A call gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to purchase the underlying asset at a predetermined rate on or before a specific date. That’s locking in the right to buy at today's price in the future. Even if it costs more when the date arrives, you still get to buy it at the agreed price.
The position was not simply bought outright. The wallet sold 400 contracts of $100,000 calls expiring in March 2027 and another 400 contracts of $90,000 calls expiring Oct. 30, collecting about $940,000 net after financing the purchase.
The second key development is the odds shifting higher. Derive’s market-implied probability of bitcoin exceeding $100,000 by Christmas rose from 9.7% a week ago to 12%. At the same time, the implied chance of bitcoin falling below $70,000 by Christmas dropped from 15.6% to 11%.
Derive is the world's largest DEX by notional volume and open interest, according to data source DefiLlama.
Still, it is much smaller than centralized giant Deribit, which has been in business for a decade and registers volume and open interest worth several billions of dollars every day. Over there, 25-delta skews for both bitcoin and ether are negative at the front end. In other words, puts are pricier than calls, indicating a bias for downside protection. Stay alert!

Strive, Inc. (ASST) acquired 6,182 bitcoin for $511.4 million between October 17 and October 23, according to an SEC filing published on Monday. The company paid an average price of $82,732 per bitcoin.
The purchase lifts Strive’s holdings to 43,000 BTC. Cash and marketable securities rose by $187.7 million to $554.6 million over the same period.
The buy comes one week after Strive closed its upsized initial public offering of SATS, its 15% Perpetual Series A Preferred Stock. The company sold 7 million shares at $90 each for $630 million in gross proceeds. Dividends accrue at 15% on a $100 stated amount, which works out to a 16.67% yield at the issue price. Payments, if declared by the board, start November 9 and land on each business day.
Strive opened the SATS offering with a $500 million target and raised the size by 2 million shares on demand. The stock trades on the Nasdaq. The company has set aside a $157.5 million dividend reserve, which covers 18 months of payments on the new shares.
JUST IN: 🇺🇸 Public company Strive purchases 6,182 Bitcoin for $511.4 million! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/5KImRceLzA
The filing disclosed a new at-the-market program under which the company can sell up to $1 billion of SATS over time. Cantor Fitzgerald, Barclays, Clear Street, StoneX, B. Riley Securities, Maxim Group and H.C. Wainwright serve as sales agents.
The structure mirrors the one Strive built for SATA, its first preferred stock, which carries a variable dividend and pays cash each business day. Strive set up a $500 million ATM for SATA in December 2025. That vehicle absorbed more than the entire daily bitcoin mining supply on a single day in May.
Under the SATS program, Strive can issue preferred shares when demand supports the price and route the proceeds into bitcoin. The company has said proceeds may fund bitcoin purchases, income-generating assets, working capital, buybacks or acquisitions.
Strive went public as a bitcoin treasury company in 2025 through a reverse merger and completed its all-stock acquisition of Semler Scientific in January, the first case of one public bitcoin treasury buying another. Holdings stood near 7,525 BTC in December 2025. The figure has since grown to more than five times that amount.
The company reported 36,818 BTC on October 20 after a purchase of 4,045 BTC between October 12 and 16. Monday’s filing adds 6,182 BTC to that total.
Strive funds its purchases through common and preferred equity and carries no debt: no bonds, no credit lines and no leveraged positions.
Chairman and CEO Matt Cole called the SATS IPO “a critical milestone in our strategy to maximize long-term total returns for our common equity investors.”
Strategy, the largest corporate holder with 848,517 BTC, proposed daily dividends across its five preferred stocks in September.

title: Galaxy says bitcoin bear market is over; now is the time to buy and hold
text: Galaxy Research is making the case for buying bitcoin even after its price fell sharply from last year’s record, pointing to a slowdown in long-term holders’ sales and a recovery above a key technical level. The benchmark cryptocurrency was trading above $80,000 on Monday, down 0.2% over 24 hours, according to The Block's bitcoin (BTC) price page. Although the asset has rebounded sharply from its June 30 low, it still sits about 36% below its October 2025 record of around $126,000. Bitcoin price. Image: The Block. Bitcoin has closed above its 50-week moving average for five straight weeks through Oct. 18, after spending 44 consecutive weeks below it, Alex Thorn, Head of Firmwide Research at Galaxy, said in a report shared with The Block on Monday. Bitcoin also tested its 200-week moving average during the decline to the June low, with its worst weekly close coming 4.7% below that level, he added. Selling pressure fades Galaxy pointed to a marked slowdown in BTC movement among older wallets. According to the firm, bitcoin in wallets that had remained untouched for at least five years moved at an average rate of 34,000 BTC a month in 2026, down from 47,000 BTC in 2025, and 67,000 BTC in 2024. About 1.11 million BTC in this age category moved since October 2024, with exchange-traded funds and public treasury companies absorbing much of the supply, per the report. Galaxy also said mounting U.S. debt and deficits strengthen bitcoin’s appeal as a hedge against currency debasement, with federal debt at $40.44 trillion and AI-related borrowing adding to credit expansion. “We believe the bottom is in, selling pressure has diminished, the debasement case has strengthened, and the crowd has left,” Thorn wrote. "Our conclusion is simple: we believe now is an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin." Thorn cautioned that Galaxy's bullish view could be challenged if BTC records a weekly close below its 50-week moving average of $76,540 and fails to recover the level within a month. The report also highlighted risks from AI, including AI-assisted hacking, but Galaxy argued that recent crypto thefts targeted exchanges, vendors, devices, or users rather than Bitcoin’s underlying protocol. The firm noted that AI does not weaken Bitcoin’s SHA-256 hash function or signature scheme. On quantum computing threats, Galaxy said no computer capable of breaking Bitcoin's cryptography currently exists, pointing to ongoing work on quantum-resistant upgrades and industry funding to address the risk.

title: Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over, Galaxy Research Says: 'Now Is an Attractive Time to Buy' - Decrypt
text:
Galaxy Digital’s head of research thinks the worst is over for Bitcoin.
In a report published Monday, Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, argued that Bitcoin’s bear market ended in June and that the asset is now in an accumulation phase. “Our conclusion is simple: we believe now is an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin,” he wrote.
The call comes as Bitcoin struggles for direction. It traded at around $80,000 on Thursday, 36% below its October 2025 high but 39% above its June 30 low. On Sunday, Bitcoin briefly slipped below $80,000 to about $79,700, according to CoinGecko.
Thorn’s case starts with the charts. Bitcoin spent 44 weeks below its 50-week moving average before reclaiming it in September, and the week ended Oct. 18 marked its fifth straight weekly close above that line. Since 2011, Bitcoin has reclaimed the average after a stretch of 20 weeks or more four times. In each case, the price never closed more than 8.4% below the reclaim level over the following year and eventually regained its prior all-time high.
The halving cycle, the roughly four-year event when rewards for Bitcoin miners are cut in half thereby reducing new supply, points the same way. The three previous cycles bottomed between 777 and 912 days after a halving, and Thursday was day 916. The latest downturn was also the shallowest on record: a 53% drop, compared with declines of 77% to 93% in past cycles.
Onchain data appears to back that up. For the first time in any bear market, Bitcoin’s market value never fell below its realized value, the average price at which every coin last moved. The ratio between the two bottomed at 1.10, compared with lows of 0.56, 0.69 and 0.75 in prior cycles.
Short-term holders, whose coins carried the recovery from $58,525, have an average cost of $74,811 and sit about 9% in profit. Yet the spent-output profit ratio, which tracks whether coins are being sold at a gain, sits at 1.009, suggesting few are cashing out.
Selling pressure is fading, too. Long-dormant coins, unmoved for five years or more, have been sold at about 34,000 BTC a month this year, half the 2024 pace. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have added 87,000 BTC since the June low after holdings fell just 11% from peak to trough while the price dropped 53%, the report found.
Thorn also argued that the macro case has strengthened. Federal debt has reached $40.44 trillion, fiscal 2026 ended with a $1.99 trillion deficit, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.31% this month, its highest since 2007. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 sits less than 1% below a record, while Bitcoin would need to rise 53% to reclaim its high.
“A bet against stocks and hard assets is a bet on fiat, the one position that makes no sense today,” Thorn wrote.
The bullish call lands in a choppy market. Spot Bitcoin ETFs swung from a $1 billion three-day inflow streak to two days of heavy outflows this week, leaving October flows in the red.
Last week’s hotter-than-expected inflation data revived bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike, and Bitcoin briefly dipped below $80,000. Higher interest rates lift Treasury yields, the return investors earn for lending to the U.S. government. A bond paying around 5% with almost no risk makes Bitcoin a harder sell, while higher rates make borrowing pricier and strengthen the dollar.
Thorn’s tripwire is a weekly close below the 50-week average, currently $76,540, that isn’t regained within a month. He also noted that Bitcoin “has proven its ability to run to at least $125k, and we see no reason why it can’t retake that level.”
Galaxy and Thorn both disclose that they hold Bitcoin.

title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80,000 Ahead of Fed Decision, Midterms - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 over the past 24 hours, as a sell-off in technology stocks and nervousness ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision weighed on risk assets.
The leading cryptocurrency fell as low as $79,332 before recovering to $80,240, down 2.5% over the past week, according to CoinGecko data. It remains about 36% below its all-time high of $126,080.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $635.5 million in net outflows on Thursday, wiping out most of the gains from a three-day run of inflows, followed by a further $137.9 million on Friday, according to SoSoValue. Even so, the funds ended the week up about $301 million, snapping a two-week losing streak, though they remain down about $314 million for October.
Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, said the drop was "primarily driven by a broader correction in global risk assets," with growing skepticism toward AI-related technology stocks a major factor.
"Investors are not necessarily questioning the long-term prospects of artificial intelligence, but rather whether current elevated valuations can be justified by future earnings and cash flows," Sun told Decrypt. Outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs and the unwinding of leveraged positions "further amplified the downward pressure," he said.
Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said Bitcoin had come under pressure alongside tech stocks. "Persistent inflation, elevated Treasury yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening have reduced enthusiasm for speculative assets," she told Decrypt.
Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at quantitative investment firm Algoz, said $80,000 was a psychologically important mark for many investors, but warned that a break below it could be misleading, given low trading volumes over weekends.
More worrying, he said, was a broader decline in trading volumes as investors pull out of altcoins and park funds in stablecoins. Bitcoin needed to hold the $82,000 level from which it launched rallies in August and September to support the bull case, and staying below it "could see a broader pullback in the coming weeks while the macro uncertainty remains," he said.
"The bull case for Bitcoin is not dead but it is keeping its head below the parapet whilst so many stray bullets are flying across the globe," Wundke added.
Sun said that if Bitcoin falls further, he sees $75,000 as a key support level to watch, and expects volatility to stay elevated.
Hathorn said the Fed's decision on Wednesday and major technology earnings "could prove just as important for Bitcoin as developments within the cryptocurrency market itself." A more hawkish Fed could strengthen the dollar and weigh on risk assets, she said, while "Bitcoin's recovery may remain fragile unless stronger institutional demand accompanies any improvement in broader market sentiment."

title: Strive closes in on second-largest corporate bitcoin treasury with $511 million purchase
text: Bitcoin treasury company Strive (ASST) increased its (BTC) holdings by 6,182 BTC between Oct. 17 and Oct. 23, bringing its total treasury to 43,000 BTC, according to an 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday. The firm is now rapidly closing in on Metaplanet and Twenty One for second and third spot among public company holders, currently sitting in fourth place. Strategy dominates the cohort with 848,517 BTC, while Metaplanet, Twenty One, and MARA make up the remainder of the top five, with 44,000 BTC, 43,514 BTC, and 35,577 BTC, respectively, per Bitcoin Treasuries data. Strive CEO Matt Cole's long-stated aim is to end the year as the second-largest public bitcoin holder. The firm now needs to acquire an average of around 105 BTC per week to surpass Metaplanet's current haul. Corporate bitcoin holdings ($5M+ of value, excluding Strategy). Image: The Block. Strive's up to $1 billion SATS at-the-market offering Strive ended Oct. 23 with $504.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, up from $317.5 million a week earlier, according to the filing. Its Class A shares outstanding increased by approximately 3.3 million to 118.1 million over the same period. The company also established an at-the-market offering program for up to $1 billion of its SATS preferred stock, according to a separate SEC filing on Monday. The proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes, including additional bitcoin purchases, working capital, and other investments, the firm said. Strive continues to hold 505,000 shares of Strategy's STRC preferred stock, valued at $50.2 million as of Oct. 23, up from $49.3 million a week earlier. The number of SATA preferred shares outstanding was little changed at around 14 million. Strive also closed its offering of 7 million SATS preferred shares on Oct. 20, bringing in roughly $630 million before expenses. The shares pay a 15% annual dividend, and the company has set aside enough to cover the first 18 months of payments.

title: Prediction Markets to Generate $1.7B for Robinhood, Exceed Crypto Revenue by 2028: Bernstein
text:
Bernstein analysts raised Robinhood’s revenue estimates through 2026 and 2028, while maintaining their HOOD price target unchanged at $160.
Bernstein analysts expect prediction markets to become one of the incremental earnings drivers for trading platform Robinhood Markets (HOOD), potentially surpassing its crypto-derived revenue.
Prediction markets could drive up to $1.7 billion in business for Robinhood by 2028, surpassing the projected $1.6 billion in crypto-based revenues for that year, according to a Bernstein analysts’ forecast shared with Cointelegraph on Monday.
The analysts expects Robinhood’s prediction market revenue to increase to $1.7 billion in 2028 from about $650 million this year, accounting for roughly 18% of Robinhood’s projected $9.4 billion in total 2028 revenue.
The forecast comes a day ahead of Robinhood’s third-quarter 2026 report and shows that prediction markets are becoming a growing revenue source for the retail-focused trading platform.
Bernstein expects Robinhood’s Q3 revenue to increase 13% quarter-over-quarter to around $1.5 billion, driven by growing equity notional volumes, options volumes, event contract volumes, along with a recovery in crypto trading volume.
Bernstein raised Robinhood’s revenue estimates by 3% for 2026, 4% for 2027 and 3% for 2028, while keeping its $160 price target unchanged, citing higher equities and crypto revenue assumptions.
The Nasdaq-traded shares were poised to open down on Monday, with premarket activity paring the stock price down to $93.60, according to Yahoo Finance. HOOD stock is down more than 29% over the past 12 months.
