title: Strategy pauses bitcoin buys, repurchases $205 million of STRC preferred shares
text: Bitcoin (BTC) treasury company Strategy (MSTR) did not buy or sell any bitcoin between Oct. 19 and Oct. 25, ending a five-week acquisition streak, according to an 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday. Strategy's bitcoin holdings therefore remain at 848,517 BTC, worth around $67.9 billion, equivalent to more than 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The haul was bought at an average price of $75,446 per bitcoin for a total cost of around $64 billion, including fees and expenses. Instead, Strategy repurchased 2.07 million STRC preferred shares last week for around $204.9 million, using its USD Cash reserve. As of Oct. 25, the firm's USD Reserve and USD Cash balances were $4.83 billion and $242.4 million, respectively, Strategy said in the filing. Strategy bitcoin holdings. Image: The Block. MSCI concerns Earlier this month, MSCI said it will adopt new rules against "non-operating" companies that could ultimately mean Strategy's MSTR stock is excluded from its indexes. Exclusion from MSCI's indexes could make it harder for Strategy to raise money to buy more bitcoin. Steve Lee, co-founder of Neoclassic Capital, previously told The Block that reduced demand from index investors could push shares closer to the value of their underlying bitcoin holdings, making it less attractive to raise funds through new stock sales. Meanwhile, Strategy dominates the 200 public companies that have adopted some form of bitcoin acquisition model. Metaplanet, Tether-backed Twenty One, Strive, and MARA make up the rest of the top five, holding 44,000 BTC, 43,514 BTC, 36,818 BTC, and 35,577 BTC, respectively, according to Bitcoin Treasuries data. Cumulative bitcoin treasuries of public companies. Image: The Block. Strategy's stock fell 6.9% last week, closing Friday at $146.02, according to The Block's MSTR price page. title: Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buying, Spends $205M Buying Back STRC - Decrypt
text:
Strategy did not buy any Bitcoin last week, breaking a run of weekly purchases that began in mid-September, as it spent $204.9 million buying back its STRC preferred stock instead, the company said on Monday.
The Bitcoin treasury firm also sold no shares through its at-the-market offering program between October 19 and 25, according to an SEC filing. It holds 848,517 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.02 billion at an average of $75,446 per coin.
Strategy has repurchased $205M of $STRC. As of 10/25/26, we hold 848,517 $BTC and $5.1B of USD Assets. $MSTRhttps://t.co/VQ9soVDIii
— Strategy (@Strategy) October 26, 2026
The pause follows a string of smaller Bitcoin purchases. Strategy bought 267 BTC for $22.1 million the previous week, after spending $21.5 million on 250 BTC the week before that and $29 million in the week it posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain.
The STRC buyback, covering 2,068,459 shares, was the largest of those weeks, up from $193.1 million the week before and $192.4 million the week prior. Strategy paid for it entirely from USD Cash, the pool of money it keeps for general purposes including buying Bitcoin, which fell to $242.4 million from $447.3 million a week earlier.
Its separate USD Reserve, which is meant to cover preferred dividends and interest on its debt, held steady at $4.83 billion. After the latest buyback, $956.8 million remains available under the company's $3 billion program for repurchasing its preferred stock, which it raised from $2 billion a week ago. A separate program to buy back MSTR common stock has $1 billion left.
The pause comes as Strategy faces possible removal from MSCI's widely tracked equity indexes. MSCI finalized a rule on October 15 that treats "non-operating companies," those whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset, as ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30. The index provider will publish the list of affected companies on November 11.
Removal would force funds that track the indexes to sell the affected shares. Strategy chairman Michael Saylor had urged MSCI to drop what he called a "discriminatory" rule.

text:
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude family of AI models, has filed for an initial public offering, the company announced on Monday.
The company plans to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT," according to its S-1 registration statement. The number of shares and the price range have not yet been set. Both Anthropic and existing shareholders will sell shares, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named first among 24 underwriters.
Anthropic has filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC related to its proposed IPO.
Read more: https://t.co/zuRMrxXzNx
Legal disclaimer: A registration statement relating to these securities has been filed with the SEC but has not yet become effective. These securities…
— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) October 26, 2026
The public filing follows a confidential draft submitted to the SEC in June. Details of that draft reported by Reuters last month included backers' hopes for a valuation above $2 trillion. In May, Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation.
Anthropic reported revenue of $16.29 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $1.16 billion in the same period a year earlier. Full-year revenue was $4.59 billion in 2025, up from $386 million in 2024 and $41 million in 2023.
The company recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion for the first half of 2026. Most of that came from a $72.4 billion charge for changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other instruments, which the filing says was primarily driven by an increase in its valuation. Its operating loss for the period was $693 million.
As of June 30, 2026, Anthropic had raised $141.1 billion in total and held $112.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents, plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments, according to the filing. As of September 30, it had more than 1,900 customers generating at least $1 million in revenue over the previous 12 months, and about 250 generating at least $10 million.
Anthropic is incorporated as a public benefit corporation, which requires its directors to balance shareholders' financial interests with those affected by its conduct and its stated purpose: "the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."
Under the proposed structure, the Long-Term Benefit Trust, a body of five financially disinterested trustees, will elect a majority of the board through a special class of stock. Immediately before the offering, Anthropic will issue a single Class F share to an entity owned by its seven co-founders, carrying 50.1% of the voting power on most shareholder matters. The filing says that makes Anthropic a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules.
Holders of Class A shares will get one vote per share. The filing warns that the structure "may effectively eliminate the ability of holders of our Class A common stock to influence important decisions, including a change in control."
Anthropic has also contributed about 847 million non-voting shares, representing 5% of its fully diluted shares as of June 30, to a wholly owned subsidiary dedicated to its public benefit purpose. Its co-founders have each pledged to give 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropic causes, according to the filing.
The company announced the fund earlier this month, drawing criticism from investor and former White House AI czar David Sacks. "Whether it serves the public good remains to be seen," he tweeted.

title: South Korea Considers Fourth Crypto Tax Delay To 2029
text:
South Korea is weighing a fourth delay of its 22% crypto tax, pushing the start from January 2027 to 2029.
South Korea’s presidential office is reviewing a fourth postponement of the country’s 22% tax on crypto gains, with a 2029 start date gaining support among lawmakers and industry groups.
The tax is scheduled to take effect January 1, 2027. The presidential office said it is in talks with government agencies about a delay, citing gaps in the regulatory framework and the problem of treating domestic and overseas trades the same way, according to Newsis reporting.
The levy dates to a 2020 amendment to the Income Tax Act. It applies a 20% national rate plus a 2% local rate to annual income from the transfer or lending of virtual assets above a 2.5 million won ($1,888) deduction. The start date was set for 2022, then pushed to 2023, 2025 and 2027 as officials conceded that tax systems and investor protections were not ready.
The argument for 2029 rests on the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, the standard under which tax authorities swap crypto transaction records with one another. South Korea is among the first group of jurisdictions set to begin exchanges in 2027. The United States does not join until 2029.
A presidential office official told Newsis that the absence of U.S. trading data is the biggest bottleneck. Without it, the National Tax Service would have to chase overseas transactions one by one, and Korean traders on domestic exchanges would carry a heavier burden than those on foreign platforms or in self-custody.
On October 16, Democratic Party lawmaker Park Min-gyu and 13 colleagues filed a bill that would push the tax to January 1 of the second year after the first international data exchange, which works out to 2029. People Power Party lawmaker Song Eon-seok filed a separate bill to strike the crypto tax provisions from the law.
The Korea Digital Asset Business Association backed the 2029 date Thursday and asked the government to pass a digital asset law with stock-market-grade investor protections before any tax takes effect.
The pressure has come from several directions at once. Last week, two public petitions, one to repeal the tax and one to defer it two years, each cleared the 50,000 signatures that force a legislative review. Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok called for a “thorough final review,” a shift for a party that had held the line on 2027.
Finance Minister Lee Hyeong-il told a parliamentary audit Thursday the government would decide “after carefully considering and gathering all opinions from the industry and the National Assembly.” Financial Services Commission chairman Lee Eog-weon said the same day that the tax should “take various circumstances into full consideration.”
The Virtual Asset User Protection Act took effect in July 2024, but the Digital Asset Basic Act, the licensing framework flagged alongside spot bitcoin ETF approval, has not passed. Lawmakers have questioned taxing a market before the law defining it exists.
The National Tax Service has not slowed down. It plans to publish a draft notice on taxable crypto income by the end of October. The government expects to settle its position through inter-agency talks after audits wrap, with a decision through National Assembly tax revisions between late November and early December.

title: Prediction markets and derivatives drive Bernstein’s crypto stock outlook for Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle
text: Crypto trading is taking a back seat to prediction markets, derivatives and tokenization in Bernstein's latest revenue outlook for Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle. In a Monday report, Bernstein kept an Outperform rating on COIN, HOOD and CRCL ahead of their third-quarter earnings. However, it slashed Coinbase's earnings forecast and price target while raising estimates for Robinhood 's revenue and Circle's earnings. Coinbase trading reset Bernstein lowered its Coinbase target to $250 from $330, pointing to weaker crypto trading volumes and a stalled recovery. Analysts Gautam Chhugani, Mahika Sapra and Sanskar Chindalia cut their 2026 revenue forecast by roughly 32% to $5.5 billion and are expecting a full-year loss of $2.60 per share versus their previous $5.97 profit. "We no longer assume any bullish crypto price action in our estimates," the analysts wrote. On the other hand, Bernstein expects prediction markets and derivatives products on Coinbase to generate roughly $2 billion in revenue by 2028, up from around $600 million earlier in the year. For the third quarter, the analysts expect spot trading to stagnate at $150 billion, with stablecoin revenue to be the biggest factor for revenue growth. Crypto trading across Robinhood and its Bitstamp subsidiary is expected to recover to roughly $50 billion, though that would still come 38% under last year's Q3 volumes at the height of the 2025 crypto bull run. Robinhood's native blockchain, which launched in July, brought in around $90 billion in transaction volume and $50 million in fees during the third quarter, coming mostly from memecoin trading. title: Bitmine buys more ETH, repurchases $46 million in shares as Tom Lee sees crypto holding up
text:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies BMNR$21.40 resumed share repurchases after a roughly 10-week pause, while adding ether ETH$2,490.55 as Chairman Tom Lee said he sees an opportunity in the recent crypto selloff.
The Ethereum treasury firm bought 2.04 million shares last week at an average price of $22.48, spending about $45.9 million. It was Bitmine's first buyback since Aug. 17, when the company wrapped up a five-week stretch of repurchases totaling roughly 21 million shares for $350 million.

The comparison follows weeks of pressure on AI-related stocks amid concerns about spending on data centers and the returns those investments might bring. Lee pointed to crypto’s smaller decline as a sign of strength, though it doesn’t rule out further losses.
Alongside the share buybacks, Bitmine picked up another 10,452 ETH worth roughly $24.5 million, slowing from 12,535 ETH the previous week.

The two purchases show how Bitmine is splitting its capital between adding more ETH and buying back its own stock, favoring the latter as the company nears its accumulation target.
Bitmine has also staked about 5.23 million ETH, or 86% of its holdings, and projects roughly $318 million in annualized staking revenue at current yields.

title: India’s CoinDCX Confirms $16 Million Loss Days After CEO Called It a ‘False Alarm’ - Decrypt
text:
Indian crypto exchange CoinDCX has admitted it lost about $16 million in an attack on its wallet infrastructure, reversing its co-founder’s earlier insistence that reports of a breach were a “false alarm.”
In a blog post, the Mumbai-based exchange said 15.99 million USDT was drained and that it has absorbed the loss itself, stressing that customer funds remain safe.
The money moved on the Tron network on Oct. 21, and the company traced the incident to a failure in an internal process meant to sweep customer deposits out of wallets it had retired after a far larger hack last year.
The disclosure caps an awkward few days for the exchange. When blockchain researchers and the Arkham tracker first flagged roughly $16 million in suspicious outflows, CEO Sumit Gupta pushed back on X, writing that CoinDCX’s wallets were “not breached” and that the flagged addresses had been compromised back in July 2025, making the activity look like “a false alarm.”
On-chain investigator ZachXBT disputed that account, noting the wallet in question had still been sweeping user deposits into CoinDCX’s current hot wallet as recently as April and May, and he urged customers to withdraw their assets.
Withdraw all funds from CoinDCX if you value your assets.
Its co-founders are clowns running a circus.
They publicly and privately denied a theft of its assets occurred meaning they straight up lied or are negligently incompetent.
Later they disclosed the $16M theft and… pic.twitter.com/uEmtogPonq
— ZachXBT (@zachxbt) October 22, 2026
The loss compounds a tumultuous stretch for one of India’s largest exchanges. CoinDCX suffered a roughly $44 million hack in July 2025 that it blamed on a server breach, prompting a bounty hunt for the stolen funds and, later, the arrest of an employee over the incident.
Together, the two episodes bring the exchange’s losses to nearly $60 million.
The retired wallets at the center of the new loss were themselves a legacy of that earlier breach, addresses the exchange had stopped using but which kept receiving residual deposits. The failure of an automated transfer system to clear them out left the funds exposed.
CoinDCX has weathered other turbulence this year. The exchange faced fraud and impersonation-scam allegations that drew a police probe, while its founder denied reports of acquisition talks with Coinbase following the 2025 hack. Coinbase has separately moved to expand across South Asia and the Middle East.
The exchange said it would share further details as its investigation continues, and reiterated that user balances are unaffected.

title: NBA becomes third league to sign CFTC prediction market pact, taps Kalshi and Polymarket
text: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the National Basketball Association have agreed to put in place standards to protect the integrity of the game amid concerns of insider trading and manipulation in prediction markets. The CFTC and NBA signed a memorandum of understanding to share information and open lines of communication about maintaining prediction markets while preserving integrity, according to a statement from the CFTC. Both Kalshi and Polymarket will be the league's "preferred prediction market exchanges," the NBA said in a statement. "As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place," said Scott Kaufman-Ross, NBA head of media distribution & partnerships, in a statement. "These partnerships represent an important step in establishing a framework that creates new opportunities to engage our fans." The NBA marks the third sports league to sign an MOU with the CFTC. Earlier this year, the National Hockey League and Major League Baseball signed similar agreements. The National Football League has not teamed up with the CFTC and has pressed the agency for tougher rules on game integrity, consumer safety and insider trading controls. The NFL has also diverged from the CFTC over when the federal or state government should regulate prediction markets. Who should regulate those billions of dollars worth of bets has become a major point of contention. The CFTC has said that most contracts on prediction markets are swaps and so fall under its "exclusive jurisdiction." However, states have argued that prediction market companies are operating illegally, violating their gaming laws and avoiding paying taxes. The fight could potentially make its way up to the U.S. Supreme Court after New Jersey asked the high court to take up the issue. Earlier this month, the NFL filed an amicus brief with the U.S. Supreme Court and said that sports contracts are gambling, so they should be overseen by states. Insider trading has also been a repeated issue in prediction markets. An active-duty U.S. Army soldier was charged in April for using confidential information to place bets on Polymarket ahead of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro's capture earlier this year. In another case, a former White House teleprompter agreed to pay more than $172,000 to settle charges that he used his advance access to President Trump 's speeches to profit on Kalshi. Kalshi and Polymarket have both said they have taken certain steps, including mandatory employment verification for traders in sensitive markets to deter insider trading.

title: NBA joins pro sports leagues on CFTC prediction markets bandwagon while NFL balks
text:
The National Basketball Association has secured a prediction markets agreement with the U.S. derivatives regulator while also penning a partnership with leading firms Kalshi and Polymarket, formally linking professional basketball into the online sports betting movement while another major organization, the National Football League, has rejected such an arrangement.
The NBA, like Major League Baseball and the National Hockey League before it, established a data-sharing memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission that oversees federal regulation of exchanges that deal with event contracts — the simple yes-or-no trades behind most sports betting. The NBA's arrangement announced Monday is said to come with constraints meant to maintain the integrity of such wagering.
At the same time, like other leagues, the NBA partnered with the top platforms as their "preferred exchanges."
"As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place," said Scott Kaufman-Ross, the NBA's head of media distribution and partnerships, in a statement. "These partnerships represent an important step in establishing a framework that creates new opportunities to engage our fans.”
The deals arrive as the prediction markets face a nationwide legal battle with several state governments that contend such betting belongs more appropriately under the power of their gambling laws. Three major federal court decisions have landed on both sides of the issue, with two of them favoring the states' argument. The U.S. Supreme Court has been asked to step in and resolve the dispute, including by the NFL, which sided with the states in a filing with the high court.
The NFL argued that the CFTC's federal oversight has been lax and understaffed, and it said the growing industry's platforms "are not subject to the same rigorous regulatory constructs and oversight provided by state gaming authorities."
Mike Selig, the CFTC chairman who has aggressively sought to bolster the industry on several paths — including legal fights with states, new regulations and these information agreements — called the NBA's decision "a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud."
Kalshi said in a Monday posting on its website that the exchange and the NBA will "share integrity data, report suspicious trading, and cooperate on investigations," adding the the arrangement "includes restrictions on permissible markets and explicit prohibitions on league and team personnel trading NBA event contracts, reinforcing our rules against insider trading and manipulation."

title: Brazil’s Stock Market Crashes After Lula’s Upset Victory - Decrypt
text:
Brazil’s stock market lost more than $200 billion in value at the open on Monday after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff, a result that prediction markets had priced at roughly a one in five chance.
The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF, ticker EWZ, a basket of Brazilian stocks that trades in New York like a single share, fell as much as 26% from Friday’s close of about $42.60, touching $31.40 before trimming the loss to about 23% at $32.84 by 10:38 a.m. ET.
That is memecoin-sized volatility for a fund built around Brazil’s biggest companies, and it leaves EWZ roughly where it started 2026 after a 34% gain through Friday.
The dollar rose as much as 12% against the real on Friday, while the Ibovespa, Brazil’s benchmark stock index, fell as much as 17% to about 170,000 points. For a dollar-based investor, those moves at their worst combine to a loss of about 26%, in line with the ETF’s low.
B3, the São Paulo exchange, halted trading for 30 minutes after the Ibovespa fell 10% from Friday’s close, its first circuit breaker since the COVID-19 pandemic. A circuit breaker is an automatic pause meant to slow panic selling, but the index kept sliding after trading resumed.
Investors had been positioning for the opposite result since Bolsonaro unexpectedly finished first in the Oct. 4 first round, with 47.03% of valid votes to Lula’s 45.16%. The Ibovespa jumped 7.85% the next day and EWZ gained more than 10% on bets that Bolsonaro would tighten public finances and open the way to lower interest rates. Monday’s drop erased that rally and, at its lows, left the Ibovespa about 11% below its Oct. 2 close.
But Lula didn’t just beat Bolsonaro, he also beat prediction markets.
Polymarket gave Bolsonaro an 82% chance of winning the day before the vote, and Kalshi had him near 80% on Sunday morning. Both platforms are prediction markets, where a contract that pays $1 if a candidate wins trades at 80 cents when traders see an 80% chance.
Polling pointed to a coin flip rather than a favorite, with the latest Datafolha survey tied at 50% each among valid votes and CNT/MDA showing Bolsonaro ahead 50.5% to 49.5% in mid-October. Lula won 51.79% to 48.21%, a margin of about 4.4 million votes, according to Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court.
Bolsonaro said on Sunday night that he does not recognize the result and will ask the courts to annul the election, after pledging in August to respect the outcome. He objected to Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting until 7 p.m. at the request of Lula’s campaign, which he said changed the rules midgame. His own campaign had separately asked for extra voting time in parts of three states.
“It is impossible to recognize the result of the elections in the context in which these things happened,” Bolsonaro said in Portuguese outside his campaign headquarters in Brasília. “We will use our legal team, we will ask for the annulment of these elections.”

title: OCC encourages community banks to issue stablecoins as federal deadline nears
text:
The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) on Monday called on community banks to enter the stablecoin market, including by applying for permission to issue their own dollar-pegged tokens.
The regulator said it wants community banks to help shape the future of payments and encouraged them to apply directly or through subsidiaries to become permitted stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.
“These opportunities complement the OCC’s Community Bank Comeback initiatives to right-size regulation and tailor supervision so community banks can grow, compete, and continue serving their communities,” said the OCC, the independent bureau of the Treasury Department that regulates and supervises national banks, federal savings associations and federal branches and agencies of foreign banks.
The invitation comes as U.S. banking groups have pressed lawmakers to restrict stablecoin yields, concerned that interest-paying tokens could draw deposits away from traditional banks. The OCC is now trying to motivate smaller lenders to enter the same market, rather than leave stablecoin payments to large banks and crypto companies.
In a separate bulletin published Oct. 21, the OCC said stablecoin issuers must comply with its newly finalized GENIUS Act regulations starting Jan. 18, 2027, when federal approval requirements take effect.
Existing issuers that submit substantially complete applications by that date may request temporary waivers allowing them to continue operating while regulators review their applications. The OCC said it generally expects to grant such waivers where appropriate.
The regulator has yet to begin accepting applications but said the process will open after the required federal paperwork approval is completed.
The OCC has recently been under fire. The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) sued it, accusing it of exceeding its legal authority in granting national trust-bank status to crypto firms.
However, the OCC’s series of trust charter approvals for crypto firms is different, as those firms do not operate under the same business model or intend to offer the same services as typical community banks, an OCC spokesperson told CoinDesk recently. Senator Elizabeth Warren asked the OCC to explain its chartering of nine crypto-focused institutions, which she argued do not meet federal regulations and constitute a risk to the financial system.

title: South Korea Weighs Another Delay on 22% Crypto Tax, Pushing to 2029
text:
The Seoul government is reportedly weighing another delay for a 2020 income tax policy on digital assets, citing concerns with receiving data from US officials.
Government officials in South Korea are reportedly weighing a delay of the country’s cryptocurrency tax policy, currently expected to be implemented in January 2027.
According to a Monday report from South Korean news outlet Newsis, the crypto income tax could be pushed to 2029 in part because it’s the earliest that officials will be able to share information on taxes related to digital asset exchanges with the US.
The policy, which would impose a 22% tax on crypto gains — 20% from income and 2% as part of a local tax — for investors earning more than 2.5 million Korean won ($1,883) annually has already seen several delays since it was first proposed in 2020.
“We are discussing postponing the implementation of virtual asset taxation,” said an official from the Blue House presidential residence.
The US is scheduled to begin participating in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework in 2029, while South Korea will implement the rules starting in 2027. A South Korean official reportedly said that the country was considering another delay for the crypto tax as the US “accounts for nearly half of the virtual asset market.”
As of Monday, South Korea’s National Tax Service listed Jan. 1, 2027 as the start date for the crypto tax.

title: Kalshi, S&P Dow Jones Partner on Prediction Market Indexes
text:
The agreement adds S&P Dow Jones gauges to a growing list of Wall Street firms expanding their involvement in prediction markets.
S&P Dow Jones Indices has partnered with prediction market platform Kalshi in a deal that will allow the exchange to offer event contracts tied to the financial index provider’s benchmarks.
According to Monday’s announcement, Kalshi will become a preferred platform for contracts linked to S&P DJI indices, with settlement based on official index values published by the company.
S&P DJI will also explore developing indexes using Kalshi’s prediction market data, potentially tracking expectations around economic developments, political outcomes and sporting events. The gauges would use prices from Kalshi’s event contracts to measure market expectations about future outcomes, rather than tracking the performance of traditional financial assets.
The companies did not disclose a timeline for either initiative. S&P DJI did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for additional details.
Related: Utah AG sues Kalshi, pursues profits from prediction market company
The agreement follows moves by traditional financial market operators into prediction markets. Intercontinental Exchange, parent of the New York Stock Exchange, committed up to $2 billion to Polymarket in October 2025.
In March, Nasdaq filed to offer prediction market-style contracts tied to the Nasdaq 100 Index, before partnering with Kalshi in August to provide market surveillance technology.
S&P Dow Jones Indices parent, S&P Global, separately announced Monday that it completed its acquisition of blockchain security firm OpenZeppelin, expanding its risk assessment capabilities for digital assets. The deal was first announced in September and financial terms were not disclosed.
OpenZeppelin provides smart contract security audits and development tools. Its open-source contract libraries underpin more than $38 trillion in value transferred, while its security team has conducted over 900 engagements, according to S&P Global.
OpenZeppelin will continue operating as its own business unit under founder Demian Brener, who will report to Yann Le Pallec, president of S&P Global Ratings.
S&P Global has also expanded its digital asset risk assessment work beyond smart contract security. Earlier this month, S&P Global Ratings launched a framework for evaluating crypto lending vaults across six risk categories, including blockchain security, liquidity and governance.

Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buys, Spends $205M On STRC
text:
Strategy skipped bitcoin buys for the week of October 19–25 and spent $204.9 million buying back its STRC preferred stock.
Strategy reported no bitcoin purchases or sales during the week of October 19 through 25. The company continues to hold 848,517 BTC, acquired for $64.02 billion at an average price of $75,446 per bitcoin.
Its cash went toward repurchasing $204.9 million of STRC preferred stock, and the firm kept a $4.83 billion cash reserve, according to a company release.
Michael Saylor’s company built its treasury into the largest corporate bitcoin holdings in the world through stock sales and convertible debt, using the proceeds to buy coins. That pattern has changed somewhat this year. The company has paused purchases several times and directed money toward buybacks of its preferred shares.
The company has had stints of pauses, from a week when the company halted its bitcoin buys to a stretch in which it sold bitcoin after five weeks without buying.
In September, the company repurchased $176 million of STRC in one week and expanded its digital credit securities repurchase program from $1 billion to $2 billion.
STRC is a preferred stock with a variable dividend, designed to trade near its $100 face value. When the shares fall below that level, as they have during recent market swings, buying them back shrinks the preferred claim. Retiring $100 of stated value for $86.52 cuts the claim by a larger amount than the cash spent, which lifts net bitcoin per share.
Bitcoin traded near $80,000 on Monday, October 26, after slipping below that level in early Asian hours. A weekend selloff pushed the price to the low $79,000’s, a level not seen in over a month.
Strategy’s average cost of $75,446 sits below that price, so the company’s holdings show a paper gain of around $3.9 billion. The $4.83 billion reserve covers preferred dividends and debt interest, according to company reporting.
Strategy’s buyback capacity depends on preferred stock trading below par and on cash from common stock sales, a funding mix that has shifted toward stock sales this year.
The company has offered no timetable for resuming bitcoin buys.

title: 'Privacy Horror’: Researcher Uncovers Extent of Samsung Smart TV User Tracking - Decrypt
text:
A researcher found that their Samsung smart TV was tracking them through several functionalities, including an "always on” microphone—and experts warn that similar tools could exist on other "everyday devices."
X user log4j claims to have reverse engineered his Samsung smart TV's firmware and discovered what they call a "privacy horror." One file called 'security-policy.xml’ featured functions including an always-on microphone, automatic content recognition, geo-positioning, network mapping, a targeted ads service, and user profile building, while Samsung TVs without a built-in microphone will look for one on connected devices such as a soundbar or Bluetooth speaker.
But a community note on the post points out that Samsung openly advertises some of these features. Its Pet Care and Family Care tools on Vision AI TVs listen for sounds like barking or crying and alert owners through the SmartThings app.
i own a relatively new (2025) samsung tv.
i kept getting weirdly targeted ads.
i tried reversing the firmware but it was aes encrypted and no keys unless tear it apart and do uart/jtag magic.
zero days it is. root shell on new samsung TVs!
discovered PRIVACY HORROR. write up? pic.twitter.com/EsxxCy1b6a
— log4j (@log4j) October 21, 2026
James Bore, a cybersecurity and technology consultant, told Decrypt that this isn't a new finding but just adding awareness to something that most people weren't aware of.
"The amount of monitoring that smart devices, from TVs to voice assistants to cars, do isn't secret as such, just not something promoted," Bore said. "If you read privacy policies and [End-User License Agreements], it's all in there in almost every case, but most people don't read those."
Jake Moore, Global Cybersecurity Advisor at cybersecurity firm ESET, told Decrypt that this could be the start of a wave of similar findings, as a trend of AI-powered reverse engineering has swept the internet.
"AI-assisted reverse engineering may make it easier and faster for researchers to uncover and explain how devices collect, process, and share data," Bore agreed, "but the underlying collection itself is generally not new or unknown."
Decrypt has reached out to Samsung for comment and will update this article should they respond.
Bore added that smart TVs are monitoring user behavior to advertise to you better and persuade you to spend money. He added that this is "far from unique” to smart TVs.
Moore noted that this might be why TVs haven't seen a noticeable price increase in recent years.
"TVs haven’t really increased in price like some products over the last two decades and that may be because customer data collection is keeping those costs down," Moore said. "Smart TVs are doing far more behind the scenes than most people realise, as many can monitor what we are watching and collect our data to build profiles for targeted advertising."
Last week, smart TV owners started using AI coding agents like Claude Code to strip ads and tracking software out of their sets. One open-source project, Cleanyourtv, now lists tested setups for 107 TV models from 37 brands, though it only fully works on Android-based TVs—not Samsung’s Tizen operating system. However, as one Decrypt writer discovered, vibe-coded solutions can end up backfiring.
Both cybersecurity experts say that the public shouldn't be uniquely concerned about the functionalities revealed on Samsung TVs. Bore said that we should be more worried about how "blasé” we've become about accepting companies "constantly profiling us to manipulate us into spending more money on things we don't need."
"The concern is how much of our data is being collected and who it’s being shared with," Moore said. "It is possible to go through TV settings to minimise the amount of data access points are being used and analysed, but saying that, privacy shouldn’t be something you have to hunt through dozens of settings to find."
Those more anxious about security claim that this form of invasive data collection is enough for them to change their behavior.
Muneeb Ali, the co-founder of Stacks, a prominent Bitcoin layer-2 network, said that he doesn't handle private crypto keys in rooms with devices.
"We were paranoid that a hacked device could record or listen in," he tweeted. "Didn’t realize the TVs were literally 1st party programmed for full-on spying. Only the paranoid survive."

PHP Flaw Shows AI ‘Vulnerability Apocalypse’ on Schedule: Immunefi CEO
text:
Mitchell Amador warned internet users that websites could remain compromised for weeks, particularly smaller websites slower to adopt the emergency upgrades.
Internet users are still vulnerable to cyber exploits stemming from the PHP vulnerability, particularly through smaller websites that could take weeks to adopt the upgrade shipped last Wednesday, according to bug bounty platform Immunefi CEO Mitchell Amador.
“This is the vulnerability apocalypse” running on schedule, where finding vulnerabilities became cheap, but fixing them remains expensive, Amador told Cointelegraph.
“For the next few weeks, treat any site you log into as if it could already be compromised,” said Amador, warning users to avoid reusing passwords and to exercise caution when connecting their cryptocurrency wallets to websites. He also urged users to revoke unrecognized token approvals.
The comments come nearly a week after the PHP Foundation acknowledged that it delayed fixing a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, due to a shortage of resources. PHP developers released emergency patches for two critical vulnerabilities on the same day, but websites still need to independently upgrade.
In an interview published by Cointelegraph in June, Amador warned that the proliferation of frontier AI models changed the cybersecurity playing field in favor of attackers, causing a “vulnerability apocalypse” that led to the resurgence in decentralized finance (DeFi) hacks.
Percentage of programs with a confirmed critical vulnerability by time live. Source: Immunefi
Immunefi is the world’s largest bug bounty platform that paid out $140 million in bounties across 650 protocols to date, according to its homepage.
Related: Cysic dangles a 10% bounty, hacker pours loot into Tornado Cash
According to Cloudflare’s CEO Matthew Prince, the network saw millions of exploit attempts in the 24 hours after the PHP vulnerabilities were publicly revealed and thousands of attempts even before their disclosure, he wrote a Thursday X post.
About one in five websites worldwide routes traffic through Cloudflare, according to the internet infrastructure company, which helps websites load faster and protect users from cyber threats.
Research service W3Techs estimates that PHP powers about 69% of websites with a known server-side programming language. The vulnerabilities may allow attackers to spread malware or inject malicious scripts into websites around the world.
The FBI’s Cyber Division also warned that the vulnerabilities may allow malicious actors to “remotely execute code in PHP core, potentially compromising sensitive data and networks,” according to a Wednesday X post.

title: Galaxy Calls The Bottom: Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over
text:
Galaxy Research says that bitcoin’s bear market ended at the June low, citing a reclaimed 50-week moving average, an exodus of hedge-fund and basis-trade sellers, rising U.S. debt, and a “blockchain, not bitcoin” sentiment shift that marked the bottom in two prior cycles.
Galaxy Research believes bitcoin’s bear market ended in June and that the asset has entered an accumulation phase, according to a research alert from the firm. “We believe now is an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin,” the report said.
Bitcoin traded near $80,000 at the time of the note, about 35% below its October 2025 high and 39% above the June 30 low. The price would need to rise 53% to retake the previous record. The S&P 500, by comparison, sits within 1% of a record set on Oct. 6.
The report lays out four arguments: technical, positioning, fundamental and sentiment.
Galaxy uses two weekly moving averages to track bitcoin’s bear markets. The 200-week average has acted as a floor in each one, and the 50-week average has acted as a ceiling, according to the firm.
Bitcoin lost the 50-week average in November 2025 and stayed below it for 44 weeks. The June low tested the 200-week average and held, with the worst weekly close coming 4.7% beneath it. Price closed back above the 50-week average in September, and the week ended Oct. 18 was the fifth consecutive weekly close above that level.
Galaxy counted 13 such reclaims since 2011 and said the outcome depended on how long price had spent below the line. The four reclaims that ended spells of 20 weeks or more were higher a year later, by between 55% and 1,497%, and none closed more than 8.4% below the reclaim level in the following 12 months. Of the nine that ended shorter spells, seven fell more than 25% within a year.
The firm said the halving cycle supports the same conclusion. Prior cycles bottomed on days 777, 889 and 912 after their halvings. Oct. 22 was day 916 of the current cycle. Galaxy said the gains that followed those lows (87x, 19x and 7.6x) have shrunk each cycle and that it does not forecast a repeat.
The current drawdown of 53% is the shallowest in bitcoin’s history, the report said, and the first in which price did not fall below the network’s realized cost basis.
The report identified basis traders and macro funds as the main sellers since the top. Asset managers’ net long position in CME bitcoin futures fell 57% from the week of the all-time high, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission data cited by Galaxy.
Leveraged funds’ net short position, which represents the futures side of the cash-and-carry trade against spot ETFs, shrank by a similar amount. The front-month basis averaged 7.9% annualized in the 30 days before the high and 4.8% in the 30 days to Oct. 21, which the firm said no longer covers the trade’s costs and risk.
Galaxy pointed to 13F filings to identify the sellers. Millennium Management, Brevan Howard, Goldman Sachs, Capula, Farallon, D. E. Shaw, Schonfeld, Symmetry and Tudor cut their spot ETF holdings by between 29% and 100% between the September 2025 and June 2026 quarter-ends, a combined 68,000 BTC.
Because total holdings across all 2,200 filers fell by 48,000 BTC, the remaining institutions added in aggregate. Morgan Stanley’s wealth management arm, Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council were among the buyers.
Spot ETF holdings dropped 11% from peak to trough while price fell 53%, and the funds have added 87,000 BTC since the June low, the report said.
Galaxy’s fundamental case centers on U.S. fiscal conditions. Federal debt reached $40.44 trillion on Oct. 20, fiscal 2026 ended with a $1.99 trillion deficit, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.31% on Oct. 5, its highest since 2007.
The firm argued that a government refinancing that debt at 5% while running 6% deficits faces pressure to inflate.
The report described AI-related borrowing, which Morgan Stanley expects to reach $570 billion this year, as a contributor to that pressure rather than a competitor for capital.
On sentiment, Galaxy compared the current environment to 2015–16 and 2018–19, when mainstream finance embraced “blockchain” and dismissed bitcoin. Both periods coincided with cycle lows. The firm said the 2026 version is “stablecoins and tokenization, not bitcoin,” citing bank pilots of tokenized deposits, the Senate’s failed cloture vote on the Clarity Act on Sept. 15, and Google searches for “bitcoin” at multiyear lows.
Galaxy set a tripwire for its view: a weekly close below the 50-week average, about $76,540, that is not regained within a month. It cited AI-enabled theft, including the $387.5 million Bitget exploit, while noting none of the incidents involved the Bitcoin protocol itself.
On quantum computing, the report said 7.1 million BTC sit in outputs with exposed public keys but that no cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists. It pointed to BIP-360’s merge into the BIP repository in February and Galaxy’s own $5 million quantum readiness commitment.
